definition_zh: 电离；电离作用；电离度（溶液中分子离解成离子的比例）
definition_en: the process in which neutral atoms or molecules lose or gain electrons and become electrically charged particles
core_image: 一支充了气体的玻璃管里，一束射线穿过，原本成对绕行的电子被撞脱，正负粒子各自向两端电极奔去
scene: 实验员把一束射线打进密闭的玻璃管，管里原本不导电的气体忽然亮起并通了电。Ionization of the gas turns an insulator into a conductor.
sceneCN: 这里 ionization 指中性原子或分子被夺走电子、变成带电粒子的过程（第 1 个义项：中性粒子生成离子的转变）；句意：气体的电离使它从绝缘体变成导体。图中可辨识物件：玻璃管、两端电极、飞散的电子、淡紫色辉光。

derivatives.zh: 由 ion 加动词后缀构成，义为「使成为离子」
由 ionize 加表示已然的形容词后缀构成，义为「已电离的」
由 ionize 加表示进行的分词后缀构成，义为「致电离的」
由 ionize 加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「产生离子的装置」

senses.title: Birth of charged particles
senses.definition: the process by which a neutral atom or molecule becomes an ion
senses.definitionCN: 中性原子或分子转变为离子的过程
senses.example: Ionization of the gas turns an insulator into a conductor.
senses.exampleCN: 气体的电离使它从绝缘体变成导体。
senses.why: The noun names the making of an ion and adds an ending that marks an action or process, so the word points to the event rather than to the particle produced.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示离子的名词加表示「动作、过程」的名词后缀构成，因此指向事件本身，而不是产物。

senses.title: Gas made able to carry current
senses.titleCN: 气体被电离后能够导电
senses.definition: the change that lets a gas, normally an insulator, carry an electric current
senses.definitionCN: 使通常绝缘的气体能够承载电流的变化
senses.example: Once ionization begins, the discharge tube carries a steady current.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦开始电离，放电管就能通过稳定电流。
senses.why: A gas conducts only when it holds free charges, so the same event that creates ions is described by what it makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 气体只有带着自由电荷才能导电，因此同一事件也从「它使什么成为可能」这一角度被命名。

senses.title: Share of molecules that have split
senses.titleCN: 已离解分子所占的比例
senses.definition: the fraction of the molecules in a solution that have separated into ions
senses.definitionCN: 溶液中已经离解为离子的分子所占的比例
senses.example: In a weak acid the degree of ionization stays small.
senses.exampleCN: 在弱酸中，电离度始终很小。
senses.why: The process is not all-or-nothing, so the word also measures how far the process has gone in a given sample.
senses.whyCN: 电离并非全有全无，因此这个词也用来衡量某一具体样品中过程进行到了什么程度。

senses.title: Energy needed to strip an electron
senses.titleCN: 剥离一个电子所需的能量
senses.definition: the minimum energy required to remove an electron from an atom or molecule
senses.definitionCN: 从原子或分子中移走一个电子所需的最小能量
senses.example: Each element has a characteristic ionization energy.
senses.exampleCN: 每种元素都有其特征性的电离能。
senses.why: Removing an electron is the first step of ionization, and the energy that step costs is named by the event it enables.
senses.whyCN: 移走电子是电离的第一步，这一步要付出的能量就借用它所促成的事件来命名。

senses.title: Electron ionization in an instrument
senses.definition: the technique of knocking electrons out of sample molecules with a beam of electrons inside a mass spectrometer
senses.definitionCN: 在质谱仪内用电子束把样品分子打出电子的技术
senses.example: Electron ionization fragments the sample into charged pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 电子电离把样品打碎成带电碎片。
senses.why: The general event is narrowed to one instrument, where the electrons are removed deliberately so the fragments can be weighed.
senses.whyCN: 一般过程被收窄到某种仪器里：那里有意打掉电子，好让碎片能被称量。

senses.title: Water ionizing itself
senses.definition: the slight, spontaneous separation of water molecules into charged parts without any added acid or base
senses.definitionCN: 不加酸或碱时，水分子自发地少量分离成带电部分
senses.example: Even pure water undergoes slight self-ionization.
senses.exampleCN: 即使纯水也会发生轻微的自电离。
senses.why: Water can act as its own source of ions, so the word is used without any external agent doing the stripping.
senses.whyCN: 水可以自己充当离子来源，因此这里不需要任何外部作用者来剥离电子。

senses.title: Ionization recorded as a signal
senses.definition: the ionization produced inside a detector, which appears as an electrical pulse or current
senses.definitionCN: 在探测器内部产生的电离，以电脉冲或电流的形式呈现
senses.example: Radiation entering the chamber produces ionization that the circuit records.
senses.exampleCN: 进入电离室的辐射产生的电离会被电路记录下来。
senses.why: Here the event is valued for its by-product: each ion pair becomes a countable electrical sign of radiation passing through.
senses.whyCN: 这里看重的是它的副产品：每一对离子都变成辐射经过的可计数电信号。

senses.title: Ionization high in the atmosphere
senses.definition: the charging of air molecules far above the ground by cosmic rays and solar radiation
senses.definitionCN: 高空空气分子被宇宙射线与太阳辐射充电的过程
senses.example: Cosmic rays cause ionization high above the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线在高空造成电离。
senses.why: The same physical event is scaled up from a laboratory tube to a whole layer of air, where the stripping agent is natural radiation.
senses.whyCN: 同一物理事件从实验室的玻璃管放大到整层空气，只是剥离电子的主角换成了天然辐射。

intro.en: Ionization is built on ion, a word coined in 1834 from a Greek participle meaning 'going', plus the action ending -ization. The dates of the derived English words are approximate.
intro.cn: ionization 由 ion 加表示动作的名词后缀构成，而 ion 是 1834 年借希腊语一个意为「行走的」分词所造的新词；英语派生词的具体年代为约数。

items.en: The Greek verb ienai meant 'to go', and its neuter participle ion named 'that which goes'; the image is a thing in motion.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 ienai 意为「走、行进」，其中性分词 ion 指「行走之物」；画面是一个在移动的东西。

items.en: Faraday, advised by Whewell, took ion for the charged particles that travel to the electrodes during electrolysis, because they appear to move through the liquid.
items.cn: 法拉第在惠威尔的建议下，用 ion 指电解时奔向电极的带电粒子，因为它们看上去是在液体中移动。

items.en: English adopted ion as the ordinary noun for an atom or molecule that carries an electric charge.
items.cn: 英语把 ion 收作普通名词，指带电荷的原子或分子。

items.en: As electrolysis and gas discharge were studied, speakers formed the verb ionize and the noun ionization from ion, using the verb and action endings already available in English.
items.cn: 随着电解与气体放电研究推进，人们用英语中现成的动词后缀与动作名词后缀，从 ion 造出动词 ionize 与名词 ionization。

items.en: Improved vacuum pumps and radiation detectors carried the word into mass spectrometry, nuclear physics and atmospheric science, where the same event is made, measured or merely observed.
items.cn: 真空泵与辐射探测器的改良把该词带入质谱、核物理与大气科学，同一事件在那里或被制造、或被测量、或只是被观察到。

items.en: Source uncertain for the pre-Greek root: the deeper origin of ienai is not established, and older forms sometimes quoted for it are reconstructions rather than attested words.
items.cn: 希腊语之前的词根来源不确定：ienai 更早的来源尚未确立，有时被引用的更古老形式属于重构形式，而非有文献的形式。

note.en: The first group shares the ion stem; the second group names neighbouring events that also leave charged particles behind.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ion 词干；第二组是同样留下带电粒子的相邻过程。

entries.definition: The charged atom or molecule that ionization produces; the noun names the result, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 电离所产生的带电原子或分子；这个名词指结果，不指过程。

entries.definition: To produce ions from neutral matter; it is the action behind the noun ionization.
entries.definitionCN: 从中性物质产生离子；它就是 ionization 背后的动作。

entries.definition: An apparatus that ionizes air; the ending marks an agent, so it names a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 使空气电离的装置；后缀标示施动者，因此它指机器。

entries.definition: A detector in which ionization is the working signal; here the word is a modifier inside a fixed term.
entries.definitionCN: 以电离作为工作信号的探测器；这里该词是固定术语里的修饰成分。

entries.definition: The separation of a molecule into smaller pieces, often ions; it stresses the breaking of a bond rather than the birth of charge.
entries.definitionCN: 分子分离成更小部分，常为离子；它强调化学键断开，而不是电荷产生。

entries.definition: A process in which an electric current forces chemical change; ionization supplies the carriers that make it work.
entries.definitionCN: 电流迫使化学变化发生的过程；电离提供使其运作的载流子。

entries.definition: The flow of current through an ionized gas, seen as glow or spark; it is the visible consequence of ionization.
entries.definitionCN: 电流通过被电离气体的现象，表现为辉光或火花；它是电离可见的后果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ion plus the action ending -ization: the noun is the event of making ions.
normal.cn: ion 加表示动作的名词后缀：这个名词就是「制造离子」这件事。

normal.en: The family runs ion, ionize, ionized, ionizing, ionizer and ionization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ion、ionize、ionized、ionizing、ionizer 与 ionization。

normal.en: Fixed terms mark the measured side: ionization energy, degree of ionization, ionization chamber.
normal.cn: 固定术语标出可测量的一面：电离能、电离度、电离室。

normal.en: Faraday chose the Greek word for 'going' because the charged pieces seem to walk toward the poles.
normal.cn: 法拉第选用了希腊语「行走」一词，因为带电碎片看上去正走向两极。

normal.en: A discharge tube is the standard picture: dark gas, a beam, then a glowing path of current.
normal.cn: 放电管是标准画面：暗气体、一束射线，然后一条发亮的通电路径。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd at a gate suddenly splitting into two streams that head for opposite exits.
abstract.cn: 想象门口的人群忽然分成两股，朝相反的两个出口走去。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door that opens only when one small pin is pulled out of its hinge.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁住的门，只因为从铰链里抽走一枚小销子就开了。

abstract.en: Picture a choir that was one voice until a single note split it into two answering parts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱队原本只有一个声音，一个音符把它分成互相应答的两部。

examples.en: The detector relies on ionization produced by passing particles.
examples.cn: 该探测器依靠粒子经过时产生的电离工作。

examples.en: Raising the temperature increased the degree of ionization in the vapour.
examples.cn: 升高温度提高了蒸气中的电离度。

examples.en: Textbooks list the ionization energies of the elements in a table.
examples.cn: 教科书用一张表列出各元素的电离能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ion（离子）+ 化」——把中性粒子化成带电离子

root: 英语 ion（离子，1834 年据希腊语 ienai「行走」的中性分词所造）+ 表示动作的名词后缀；希腊语更早的词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one event: a neutral particle is stripped of charge, and the same event is then read as conductivity, as a measured share, as an energy cost, as an instrument technique, as water acting on itself, as a detector signal, and as a natural process in the sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一件事：中性粒子被剥去电荷；同一件事随后被读成导电能力、被量化的比例、能量代价、仪器手段、水对自身的作用、探测器信号，以及天空中的自然过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam crossing a sealed tube, knocking electrons loose so that charged pieces fly to opposite poles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束射线穿过密闭管，把电子撞脱，带电碎片飞向相反的两极。

branches.en: THE EVENT ITSELF: a neutral particle becomes charged, which is the gesture every other sense repeats.
branches.cn: 事件本身：中性粒子变成带电粒子，这是其余各义项反复重演的那个动作。

branches.en: WHAT IT ENABLES AND HOW FAR IT GOES: the gas can carry current, and the process can be reported as a proportion.
branches.cn: 它促成了什么、又进行到哪一步：气体因此能导电，过程也能被报成一个比例。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF THE FIRST STEP: stripping one electron has a fixed energy cost named after the event.
branches.cn: 第一步的代价：剥走一个电子要付出固定能量，这笔能量便以该事件命名。

branches.en: WHO DOES THE STRIPPING: an electron beam in a machine, or water molecules acting on themselves.
branches.cn: 谁来完成剥离：机器里的电子束，或水分子对自身下手。

branches.en: WHERE THE EVENT IS READ: the ion pairs become a signal in a chamber, or a natural charge layer high in the air.
branches.cn: 事件在哪里被读取：离子对在电离室里变成信号，或在高空形成天然带电层。

intro.en: Ionization is a Greek-rooted noun with two layers of endings, and both layers also build other English words.
intro.cn: ionization 是一个希腊语词根的名词，带着两层词尾，这两层词尾也参与构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, not Latin; Latin contributes only the verb ending that reached English through French, so no Latin cognate of the root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语；拉丁语只贡献了经法语进入英语的动词词尾，因此不列出该词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The particle itself is the noun ion.
items.exampleCN: 粒子本身就叫 ion。

items.structure: verb-forming ending, through French from Greek
items.example: The ending turns the noun into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成动作。

items.structure: action noun ending, from the verb ending plus a noun ending
items.meaning: the process of making or becoming
items.example: The longer ending names the process rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 较长的词尾命名过程而不是单次动作。

items.example: The beam ionizes the gas in the tube.
items.exampleCN: 射束使管中的气体电离。

items.structure: ionize plus the action noun ending
items.example: Ionization of the gas turns it into a conductor.
items.exampleCN: 气体的电离使它成为导体。

items.example: The ionized layer reflects radio waves.
items.exampleCN: 已电离的那一层会反射无线电波。

items.example: Ionizing radiation is handled behind shielding.
items.exampleCN: 致电离辐射要在屏蔽层后操作。

items.example: The ionizer charges the air in the room.
items.exampleCN: 这台离子发生器使室内空气带电。

definition_zh: 使电离；电离（使中性原子或分子变成离子）；被电离
definition_en: to make neutral atoms or molecules become ions, or to become ionic in this way
core_image: 车间里一排塑料件通过高压区，表面分子被扯出电子，细小的带电雾落在表面，油墨终于挂住
scene: 印刷前，工人让塑料片穿过高压电场，表面因此带上电荷，油墨才不再滑开。A high-voltage field can ionize the surface molecules so that ink grips.
sceneCN: 这里 ionize 指用外部作用把中性分子变成带电离子（第 1 个义项：使某物电离）；句意：高压电场能使表面分子电离，好让油墨附着。图中可辨识物件：高压电极、塑料片、带电雾、印好的图案。

senses.title: Strip electrons from neutral matter
senses.titleCN: 从中性物质中剥出电子
senses.definition: to make neutral atoms or molecules become ions by removing or adding electrons
senses.definitionCN: 通过移走或加上电子，使中性原子或分子变成离子
senses.example: A high-voltage field can ionize the surface molecules so that ink grips.
senses.exampleCN: 高压电场能使表面分子电离，好让油墨附着。
senses.why: The verb carries the plain causative reading: an outside agent acts on matter, and the result is ions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词携带直白的致使义：外部作用者施力于物质，结果就是离子。

senses.title: Become ionic without an agent
senses.definition: to undergo ionization naturally, as a gas or liquid does when conditions allow
senses.definitionCN: 在条件允许时像气体或液体那样自然发生电离
senses.example: At very high temperatures the vapour begins to ionize on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 在极高温度下，蒸气开始自行电离。
senses.why: The same event is viewed without an agent, so the verb shifts to the intransitive pattern: the substance simply undergoes the change.
senses.whyCN: 同一事件在不提作用者时被观察，于是动词转为不及物：物质自身经历这一变化。

senses.title: Make a gas conduct
senses.definition: to create free charges in a gas so that it can carry a current
senses.definitionCN: 在气体中产生自由电荷，使其能够承载电流
senses.example: A spark first ionizes the air, and then the arc can jump.
senses.exampleCN: 火花先使空气电离，电弧随后才能跳过。
senses.why: Ionizing a gas is usually done to change what the gas can do; the purpose is conductivity, not the ions themselves.
senses.whyCN: 使气体电离通常是为了改变气体的能力；要点是导电，而不是离子本身。

senses.title: Split water or acid molecules
senses.definition: to cause water or an acid to separate into charged parts in solution
senses.definitionCN: 使水或酸在溶液中分离成带电部分
senses.example: Water ionizes only slightly unless an acid is present.
senses.exampleCN: 除非有酸存在，水只会轻微电离。
senses.why: The object here is a molecule that splits rather than a gas that is struck, and the verb still means the coming-into-being of ions.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对象是发生分裂的分子，而不是被撞击的气体，动词仍指离子的产生。

senses.title: Ionize by radiation
senses.definition: to knock electrons out of matter with high-energy particles or rays
senses.definitionCN: 用高能粒子或射线把电子从物质中打出
senses.example: Cosmic rays ionize the upper atmosphere every day.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线每天都在使高层大气电离。
senses.why: Radiation is the classic natural agent of the change, so the verb routinely takes radiation as the unstated doer.
senses.whyCN: 辐射是这一变化最典型的天然作用者，因此动词常以辐射为不言自明的主角。

senses.title: Ionize a sample inside an instrument
senses.definition: to charge sample molecules in a mass spectrometer so their fragments can be measured
senses.definitionCN: 在质谱仪中使样品分子带电，以便测量其碎片
senses.example: The instrument ionizes the sample before the fragments are weighed.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器先使样品电离，然后称量碎片。
senses.why: Instrument ionizing is deliberate and repeated, turning the verb into a step in a procedure rather than a natural event.
senses.whyCN: 仪器中的电离是有意反复执行的，于是动词变成流程里的一个步骤，而非自然事件。

senses.title: Ionize atoms in a hot flame
senses.titleCN: 在高温火焰中使原子电离
senses.definition: to charge atoms thermally in a flame or arc for spectroscopy
senses.definitionCN: 在火焰或电弧中借高温使原子带电，用于光谱分析
senses.example: The flame ionizes a fraction of the atoms before they emit light.
senses.exampleCN: 火焰在原子发光前先使其中一部分电离。
senses.why: Heat is another agent of the same change, and the verb keeps its plain sense while the setting becomes an analytical burner.
senses.whyCN: 热是同一变化的另一种作用者；环境换成分析用燃烧器，动词的含义仍旧朴素。

senses.title: Ionize a surface for treatment
senses.titleCN: 为表面处理而使之电离
senses.definition: to charge the molecules on a surface so that coatings, inks or films adhere properly
senses.definitionCN: 使表面分子带电，好让涂层、油墨或薄膜正常附着
senses.example: Factories ionize plastic film so that printed layers do not peel off.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂使塑料薄膜电离，好让印上去的层不脱落。
senses.why: The industrial use applies the event to a flat object, and the aim is adhesion rather than conductivity or measurement.
senses.whyCN: 工业用法把这一事件用在平面上，目的既不是导电也不是测量，而是附着。

intro.en: Ionize is a nineteenth-century English verb built on ion, itself coined in 1834 from a Greek participle meaning 'going'. Its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: ionize 是 19 世纪在 ion 基础上构成的英语动词，而 ion 本身是 1834 年据一个意为「行走的」希腊语分词所造；其首见年代为约数。

items.en: The Greek verb ienai 'to go' supplied the participle ion, literally 'that which goes', which Faraday used for the charged particles drifting to the poles.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 ienai「走」提供了分词 ion，字面是「行走之物」，法拉第用它指漂向两极的带电粒子。

items.en: Once ion had become the ordinary English noun for a charged particle, speakers had a base for a verb of making such particles.
items.cn: ion 一旦成为指带电粒子的普通英语名词，人们就有了造出「制造此类粒子」动词的基础。

items.en: The ending -ize reached English through French and ultimately Greek, and it turns a noun into the action of producing or becoming that noun.
items.cn: 动词词尾经法语上溯至希腊语进入英语，其作用是把名词变成「产出该物或变成该物」的动作。

items.en: The verb appeared in the middle of the nineteenth century as the study of electrolysis and electrical discharge expanded; the earliest citation is not securely fixed.
items.cn: 这个动词出现在 19 世纪中叶，正值电解与放电研究扩展之时；最早的引文年代并未确凿固定。

items.en: Mass spectrometry, radiation medicine and plasma physics made the verb a routine technical step, and compound uses such as ionizing radiation followed.
items.cn: 质谱、放射医学与等离子体物理使它成为常规技术步骤，致电离辐射一类的复合用法随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain for the deeper root: the pre-Greek origin of ienai is not established, and any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 更深词根来源不确定：ienai 在希腊语之前的来源尚未确立，为它引用的更古老形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group shares the ion stem but differs in what kind of word each is; the second group describes other ways of breaking matter into charged parts.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ion 词干，但各词所属的词类不同；第二组描述把物质拆成带电部分的其他方式。

entries.definition: The charged particle that results; it cannot take an object and names no action.
entries.definitionCN: 由此产生的带电粒子；它不能带宾语，也不命名动作。

entries.definition: The event of producing ions; the verb ionize is what one does to bring it about.
entries.definitionCN: 产生离子的事件；而 ionize 是促成它时所做的动作。

entries.definition: An adjective or participle describing matter that has already acquired charge, not the act of charging it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或分词，描述已经带上电荷的物质，而不是使其带电的动作。

entries.definition: A machine that performs the ionizing; it names the doer, while the verb names the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 执行电离的机器；它命名施动者，而动词命名动作。

entries.definition: To break a molecule into smaller parts, often charged ones; the emphasis is on the severed bond, not on the resulting charge.
entries.definitionCN: 把分子拆成更小、常带电的部分；重点在断开的键，不在产生的电荷。

entries.definition: To supply electric charge to an object; it can be done without changing the object into ions.
entries.definitionCN: 给物体提供电荷；这样做并不必然把物体变成离子。

entries.definition: To decompose a substance by passing a current through it; ionization supplies the carriers, but current does the forcing.
entries.definitionCN: 通电流使物质分解；电离提供载流子，但施力的是电流。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ion plus the verb ending -ize: to make ions.
normal.cn: ion 加动词词尾：使成为离子。

normal.en: The family runs ion, ionize, ionized, ionizing, ionizer, ionization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ion、ionize、ionized、ionizing、ionizer、ionization。

normal.en: Typical objects in fixed phrases: ionize a gas, ionize the air, ionize molecules.
normal.cn: 固定搭配里的典型宾语：使气体电离、使空气电离、使分子电离。

normal.en: Radiation is the natural doer: cosmic rays ionize the upper air.
normal.cn: 辐射是天然作用者：宇宙射线使高层大气电离。

normal.en: Industry ionizes surfaces so that ink and coatings stick.
normal.cn: 工业上使表面电离，好让油墨与涂层附着。

abstract.en: Picture a comb rubbed until it pulls scraps of paper toward itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梳子被摩擦到能把纸屑吸向自己。

abstract.en: Picture a lock that opens only after one small part is flicked out of place.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁，只有把一个小零件弹离原位才打得开。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond touched at one point until ripples carry outward in rings.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭静水在一点被触动，涟漪一圈圈向外传开。

examples.en: Gamma rays ionize the molecules they pass through.
examples.cn: 伽马射线会使其穿过的分子电离。

examples.en: The technician ionized the sample with a beam of electrons.
examples.cn: 技术员用电子束使样品电离。

examples.en: Certain plastics are ionized before they are printed.
examples.cn: 某些塑料在印刷前要经过电离处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ion（离子）+ ize（使）」——使东西变成离子

root: 英语 ion（1834 年据希腊语 ienai「行走」的中性分词所造）+ 动词词尾；更早词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of stripping charge: the plain act with an agent, the act without one, the gas made conductive, water and acids split, radiation as doer, the instrument step, the hot flame, and the industrial surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个剥离电荷的动作：有作用者的直白动作、无作用者的自变、气体变得导电、水与酸离解、以辐射为作用者、仪器步骤、高温火焰与工业表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a charged field pulls electrons off a surface, and loose charged specks settle where they are wanted.
core.cn: 核心意象：带电电场把电子从表面扯下，散开的带电微粒落在需要它们的地方。

branches.en: THE ACT WITH OR WITHOUT A DOER: something strips the charge, or the substance does it on its own.
branches.cn: 有作用者与无作用者的动作：要么外物剥去电荷，要么物质自己完成。

branches.en: WHY IT IS DONE: free charges are created so that a gas can at last carry a current.
branches.cn: 为何要做：造出自由电荷，好让气体终于能承载电流。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE INSTEAD: water and acids split into charged parts inside a solution.
branches.cn: 换成分子：水与酸在溶液里分裂成带电部分。

branches.en: THE AGENTS: rays and heat do the stripping, one natural and one industrial.
branches.cn: 作用者：射线与高温完成剥离，一个天然，一个工业。

branches.en: THE SETTINGS: a mass spectrometer charges a sample, and a factory charges a film so that ink holds.
branches.cn: 场景：质谱仪使样品带电，工厂使薄膜带电好让油墨附着。

intro.en: Ionize is one root plus one ending, and the same ending recurs across thousands of English verbs.
intro.cn: ionize 由一个词根加一个词尾构成，而这个词尾出现在成千上万个英语动词里。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek; Latin only supplies the verb ending that reached English through French, so no Latin cognate of the root is given.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语；拉丁语只提供了经法语进入英语的动词词尾，因此不列出词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The noun ion names the product of the act.
items.exampleCN: 名词 ion 命名这一动作的产物。

items.structure: verb-forming ending, through French from Greek
items.example: The ending turns a noun into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成「制造」类动词。

items.meaning: the process of making or becoming
items.example: The noun ending turns the act into a process.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾把动作变成过程。

items.example: The field ionizes the surface.
items.exampleCN: 电场使表面电离。

items.example: The ionized film holds the ink.
items.exampleCN: 经过电离的薄膜能挂住油墨。

items.example: Ionizing rays need shielding.
items.exampleCN: 致电离射线需要屏蔽。

items.example: The ionizer charges the air.
items.exampleCN: 离子发生器使空气带电。

items.structure: ionize plus the action noun ending
items.meaningCN: 使物质成为离子的过程
items.example: Ionization raises the conductivity of the gas.
items.exampleCN: 电离提高了气体的导电性。

derivatives.zh: 由 ionize 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「电离过程」
由 ionize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已电离的」

definition_zh: 氧化；氧化作用；氧化（失去电子或氧化数升高的过程）
definition_en: the process in which a substance combines with oxygen or loses electrons, so its oxidation state rises
core_image: 一块新切的铁板放在潮气里，先起橘红薄斑，再连成松软的壳，亮面被一层氧化层吃掉
scene: 海边仓库里的铁板放了一个月，接缝处先冒出橘色斑点，随后整片被一层松脆的壳盖住。Oxidation of the iron plates left a loose orange crust.
sceneCN: 这里 oxidation 指物质与氧结合、表面生成氧化物的过程（第 1 个义项：与氧化合成氧化物）；句意：铁板的氧化留下一层松脆的橘色外壳。图中可辨识物件：铁板、锈斑、潮湿空气、剥落的薄壳。

derivatives.zh: 由 oxide 加动词词尾构成，义为「使氧化」
由 oxidize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已氧化的」
由 oxidize 加进行词尾构成，义为「有氧化能力的」
由 oxidize 加施动词尾构成，义为「氧化剂」

senses.title: Combining with oxygen
senses.definition: the process in which a substance combines with oxygen to form an oxide
senses.definitionCN: 物质与氧结合形成氧化物的过程
senses.example: Oxidation of the iron plates left a loose orange crust.
senses.exampleCN: 铁板的氧化留下一层松脆的橘色外壳。
senses.why: The word was named for oxygen itself, so its oldest sense is the literal joining of a substance with that gas.
senses.whyCN: 这个词正是以氧命名，因此最早的义项就是物质与那种气体字面意义上的结合。

senses.title: Losing electrons
senses.definition: the loss of electrons by an atom, ion or molecule during a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 原子、离子或分子在反应中失去电子的过程
senses.example: Each iron atom undergoes oxidation and gives up two electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 每个铁原子发生氧化，让出两个电子。
senses.why: Once chemists understood charge transfer, the oxygen-based name was kept for a wider class: whatever loses electrons counts as oxidized.
senses.whyCN: 化学家弄清电荷转移之后，这个以氧命名的说法被保留给更大的一类过程：凡是失去电子的都算被氧化。

senses.title: Rise in oxidation number
senses.definition: any change that increases the oxidation number of an element, whether or not free oxygen is involved
senses.definitionCN: 使某元素的氧化数升高的任何变化，无论是否涉及游离氧
senses.example: The oxidation number of sulfur rises from four to six in this step.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一步里，硫的氧化数从四升到六。
senses.why: The bookkeeping sense turns the reaction into a number that can be tracked, so oxidation becomes a shift in that number.
senses.whyCN: 这种记账式理解把反应变成可追踪的数字，于是氧化就表现为该数字的移动。

senses.title: Metal corroding in air
senses.definition: the slow attack of a metal surface by air and moisture, producing rust, tarnish or scale
senses.definitionCN: 金属表面被空气与水分缓慢侵蚀，生成锈、暗斑或氧化皮
senses.example: Roof sheets in coastal towns show heavy oxidation within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海城镇的屋面板一年之内就出现严重氧化。
senses.why: The common sense narrows the reaction to the visible damage people actually notice on tools and structures.
senses.whyCN: 日常义把反应收窄到人们在工具与建筑上真正看得见的损坏。

senses.title: Food and oil going stale
senses.definition: the reaction of fats, oils or food with oxygen that makes them rancid, dark or stale
senses.definitionCN: 脂肪、油或食物与氧反应而变哈喇、变暗或变陈
senses.example: Proper packaging slows the oxidation of cooking oil.
senses.exampleCN: 合适的包装能减缓食用油的氧化。
senses.why: The same chemical event shows up as an off smell in the kitchen, so the word names spoilage as well as corrosion.
senses.whyCN: 同一化学事件在厨房里表现为异味，因此这个词也用来命名食物的败坏。

senses.title: Energy release in living cells
senses.definition: the breakdown of nutrients with oxygen in cells to release usable energy
senses.definitionCN: 细胞中营养物质与氧一起分解、释放可用能量的过程
senses.example: Beta oxidation in the liver breaks fatty acids into smaller units.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏中的 β 氧化把脂肪酸拆成更小的单位。
senses.why: Biology applies the reaction to fuel inside the body, where oxidation is the source of energy rather than damage.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这一反应用在体内燃料上，那里氧化是能量来源，而不是损坏。

senses.title: Burning as fast oxidation
senses.definition: rapid combination with oxygen that releases heat and light
senses.definitionCN: 与氧迅速结合并放出热与光
senses.example: Combustion is simply rapid oxidation with a visible flame.
senses.exampleCN: 燃烧不过是带可见火焰的快速氧化。
senses.why: Fire was the original dramatic example of combining with oxygen, so burning is classified as the fast end of the same scale.
senses.whyCN: 火是与氧结合最戏剧化的原始例证，因此燃烧被归为同一尺度上最快的一端。

senses.title: Deliberate oxidation in industry
senses.titleCN: 工业上刻意进行的氧化
senses.definition: a controlled reaction with oxygen used to bleach, purify or manufacture a product
senses.definitionCN: 为漂白、提纯或制造产品而有意控制的与氧反应
senses.example: The plant uses partial oxidation to turn methane into useful gases.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂用部分氧化把甲烷转成有用的气体。
senses.why: When the reaction is chosen and controlled, oxidation stops being decay and becomes a manufacturing step.
senses.whyCN: 当反应被挑选并受控时，氧化就不再是衰败，而成了制造工序。

intro.en: Oxidation is built on oxygen, a French coinage of 1777 made from Greek words for 'sharp' and 'born'. Its first recorded dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oxidation 由 oxygen 派生，而 oxygen 是 1777 年的法语新造词，取自希腊语表示「尖锐」与「出生」的两个词；各词首见年代为约数。

items.en: Greek oxys meant 'sharp' or 'sour', the quality of acids; it belongs with the verb oxein 'to sharpen', and the notion of a cutting taste runs through both.
items.cn: 希腊语 oxys 意为「尖锐、酸」，指酸的性质；它与动词 oxein「使尖锐」同族，「割舌的味道」这一念头贯穿两者。

items.en: The combining form -genes meant 'born' or 'producing', so a compound built with it names something that generates what the first part names.
items.cn: 构词成分 -genes 意为「出生、产生」，用它构成的复合词指生成前一部分所指之物。

items.en: Lavoisier named the newly isolated gas oxygène, literally 'acid-producing', because he held that this gas was necessary for the formation of acids.
items.cn: 拉瓦锡把新分离出的气体命名为 oxygène，字面是「产酸的」，因为他认为这种气体是酸形成的必要成分。

items.en: English adopted the French name at the end of the eighteenth century, replacing the older descriptive label for the same gas.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪末采用这个法语名称，取代了此前对同一气体的描述性叫法。

items.en: Oxide was formed for a compound with oxygen, and oxidation followed as the noun of the process; oxidize was built on oxide with the ordinary verb ending.
items.cn: oxide 被用来指与氧形成的化合物，oxidation 随后成为指该过程的名词；oxidize 则是在 oxide 上加普通动词词尾构成。

items.en: With the electron theory of valence, chemists generalised the term: loss of electrons, and later any rise in oxidation number, became the defining test rather than the presence of oxygen.
items.cn: 随着价键的电子理论，化学家把该词一般化：判定标准变成失去电子、以及后来任何氧化数升高，而不再是有没有氧参与。

note.en: The first group shares the oxygen-derived stem; the second group names neighbouring changes that are often paired with oxidation in the same reaction.
note.cn: 第一组共享由氧派生的词干；第二组是同一反应里常与氧化配对出现的相邻变化。

entries.definition: To cause oxidation or to undergo it; the noun names the event, the verb names the acting or the changing.
entries.definitionCN: 使氧化或自身被氧化；名词命名事件，动词命名施动或变化本身。

entries.definition: A compound of oxygen with another element; it is the product, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 氧与另一元素形成的化合物；它是产物，不是过程。

entries.definition: The substance that brings about oxidation by accepting electrons; it is an agent, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 通过接受电子促成氧化的物质；它是作用者，不是事件。

entries.definition: Another word for the electron-accepting substance, common in rocketry and safety writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指接受电子的物质的另一种说法，常见于火箭与安全领域。

entries.definition: The gain of electrons or the lowering of an oxidation number; it always accompanies oxidation in a closed system.
entries.definitionCN: 获得电子或氧化数降低；在封闭体系里它总与氧化同时发生。

entries.definition: The slow eating away of a metal by its surroundings; oxidation is often its cause, but the word describes the damage.
entries.definitionCN: 金属被周围环境缓慢侵蚀；氧化常是其原因，但这个词描述的是损坏。

entries.definition: The particular oxidation of iron in damp air that produces reddish flakes; it is narrower than oxidation.
entries.definitionCN: 铁在潮湿空气中生成红色薄片的那一种氧化；比氧化窄得多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The stem comes from oxygen, so the noun first meant the act of oxygen joining a substance.
normal.cn: 词干来自氧，因此这个名词最初指氧与物质结合的动作。

normal.en: The family runs oxide, oxidize, oxidized, oxidizing, oxidizer, oxidation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oxide、oxidize、oxidized、oxidizing、oxidizer、oxidation。

normal.en: Bookkeeping terms mark the modern sense: oxidation state, oxidation number.
normal.cn: 记账式术语标出现代义：氧化态、氧化数。

normal.en: Living cells run the same reaction as a source of energy, not as damage.
normal.cn: 活细胞把同一反应当作能量来源，而不是损坏。

normal.en: Fire is the fast end of the scale, rust the slow end.
normal.cn: 火是这一尺度上快的一端，锈是慢的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a bright coin left on a sill until a dull film grows over its face.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚亮硬币留在窗台上，直到表面长出一层暗膜。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed jar of nuts whose air slowly turns them bitter without any visible change.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐密封坚果，里面的空气让它们慢慢变苦，却看不出明显变化。

abstract.en: Picture a runner burning through stored fuel and later feeling the same warmth in the kitchen stove.
abstract.cn: 想象跑步者烧掉体内储存的燃料，随后又在厨房炉子上感到同一种热。

examples.en: The label warns that oxidation will darken the juice within hours.
examples.cn: 标签提醒说氧化会让果汁在几小时内变深。

examples.en: Chemists balance the equation by tracking oxidation numbers.
examples.cn: 化学家通过追踪氧化数来配平方程式。

examples.en: Oxidation of the alloy began at the grain boundaries.
examples.cn: 这种合金的氧化从晶界开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oxi（氧）+ dation（做）」——氧上身的过程，就是氧化

root: 英语 oxygen（1777 年法语新造，取自希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」+ -genes「产生」）+ 表示过程的名词词尾；首见年代多为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one joining with oxygen and then a wider loss of electrons: the plain combination, electron loss, a rising number, metal decay, stale food, energy in cells, fire, and controlled manufacture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个「与氧结合」出发，再扩展到失去电子：字面结合、失电子、氧化数升高、金属衰败、食物变陈、细胞产能、火，以及受控的制造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright metal face dulling under a growing crust of oxide.
core.cn: 核心意象：明亮的金属面在渐厚的氧化层下失去光泽。

branches.en: THE LITERAL JOINING: oxygen attaches to the substance, which is where the name began.
branches.cn: 字面结合：氧附着到物质上，名称正起源于此。

branches.en: THE GENERALISED TEST: electrons leave and the oxidation number climbs, whether or not free oxygen is present.
branches.cn: 一般化的判据：电子离去、氧化数上升，无论有没有游离氧。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE COST: a metal face dulls, flakes or scales where the reaction is allowed to run.
branches.cn: 看得见的代价：反应放任进行之处，金属面变暗、起皮或结垢。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN AND THE PLANT: the same reaction spoils oil or is deliberately turned into a product.
branches.cn: 厨房与工厂：同一反应要么弄坏油，要么被刻意做成品。

branches.en: THE ENERGY SIDE: cells and flames both release energy by the same loss of electrons.
branches.cn: 能量这一面：细胞与火焰都靠同样的失电子释放能量。

intro.en: Oxidation is a noun built on a Greek-derived scientific name plus two common endings, and the whole family shares that stem.
intro.cn: oxidation 由希腊语来源的科学名称加两层常见词尾构成，整个词族共享这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Greek in origin, though it reached English through French scientific naming; Latin contributes only the verb and noun endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干源自希腊语，经法语科学命名进入英语；拉丁语只贡献动词与名词词尾，因此不列出该词根的拉丁同族词。

scene: 铁钉在潮湿的棚子里放了几周，表面起了一层橘红薄壳。Damp air will oxidize the nails within weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 oxidize 指使金属与氧结合、表面生成氧化物（第 1 个义项：使与氧结合）；句意：潮湿空气会让这些钉子几周内氧化。图中可辨识物件：铁钉、锈壳、漏雨的棚顶、接雨的盆。

senses.title: Make a substance combine with oxygen
senses.definition: to cause a substance to combine with oxygen and form an oxide
senses.definitionCN: 使物质与氧结合并形成氧化物
senses.example: Damp air will oxidize the nails within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿空气会让这些钉子几周内氧化。
senses.why: The verb is the working form of the oxygen-based name: an agent, or the air itself, brings the gas into combination.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是以氧命名的那个词的动作形式：某个作用者，或者空气本身，促使这种气体与物质结合。

senses.title: Strip electrons from something
senses.definition: to remove electrons from an atom, ion or molecule, raising its oxidation state
senses.definitionCN: 从原子、离子或分子中移走电子，使其氧化态升高
senses.example: The reagent oxidizes the alcohol to an aldehyde.
senses.exampleCN: 该试剂把醇氧化成醛。
senses.why: Once oxidation meant any loss of electrons, the verb took on the transitive reading of forcing that loss on something.
senses.whyCN: 当氧化泛指任何失电子之后，这个动词就带上「迫使某物失电子」的及物含义。

senses.title: Rust or tarnish on its own
senses.definition: to undergo slow surface corrosion in air, without a named agent
senses.definitionCN: 在空气中缓慢发生表面腐蚀，不点明作用者
senses.example: Silver oxidizes quickly in air that contains sulfur compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 银在含硫化合物的空气中很快氧化变暗。
senses.why: Everyday observation has no experimenter, only a metal and the weather, so the verb commonly appears without an agent.
senses.whyCN: 日常观察里没有实验者，只有金属与天气，因此这个动词常以不带作用者的形式出现。

senses.title: Food or drink turning stale
senses.definition: to spoil through contact with air, as fats, wine or cut fruit do
senses.definitionCN: 因接触空气而败坏，如脂肪、葡萄酒或切开的水果
senses.example: Left uncovered, the wine oxidizes and loses its freshness.
senses.exampleCN: 敞着不放，葡萄酒会氧化并失去新鲜感。
senses.why: The kitchen applies the verb to flavours rather than surfaces, but the cause is the same combination with oxygen.
senses.whyCN: 厨房把这个动词用在味道而不是表面，但成因仍是同一种与氧的结合。

senses.title: Break down fuel in the body
senses.definition: to convert fats, sugars or other nutrients into smaller units with the help of oxygen in cells
senses.definitionCN: 在细胞中借助氧把脂肪、糖等营养物转成更小单位
senses.example: Muscles oxidize glucose during long exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间运动时肌肉会氧化葡萄糖。
senses.why: Physiology treats the reaction as the body's way of extracting energy, so the verb can name what cells do to fuel.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这一反应视为身体提取能量的方式，因此这个动词可以指细胞对燃料所做的事。

senses.title: Raise an element to a higher valence
senses.titleCN: 把元素氧化到更高价态
senses.definition: to convert an element into a compound in which it has a higher oxidation number
senses.definitionCN: 使某元素转成氧化数更高的化合物
senses.example: The process oxidizes sulfur dioxide into the trioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 该过程把二氧化硫氧化成三氧化硫。
senses.why: In chemical writing the verb marks a direction on the number scale rather than the visible decay of a surface.
senses.whyCN: 在化学写作里，这个动词标出数字尺度上的方向，而不是表面的可见衰败。

senses.title: Grow a protective oxide layer
senses.definition: to form a thin oxide film on a surface on purpose, so that further damage is slowed
senses.definitionCN: 有意在表面生成薄氧化膜，从而减缓进一步损坏
senses.example: Engineers oxidize the aluminium panel to harden its skin.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师对铝板作氧化处理，使其表层变硬。
senses.why: The same reaction is turned to advantage: the crust that ruins iron can, on another metal, seal the surface.
senses.whyCN: 同一反应被转为有利：毁掉铁的那层壳，换到另一种金属上却能封住表面。

senses.title: Bleach or deactivate by oxidation
senses.definition: to use oxidation to remove colour or to destroy an unwanted substance
senses.definitionCN: 利用氧化去除颜色或破坏不需要的物质
senses.example: The mill oxidizes the dye so that the cloth comes out pale.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把染料氧化，使布匹变浅。
senses.why: Here the electron loss is valued for its side effect: colour and unwanted compounds are broken down rather than the metal being consumed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的失电子看重的是副作用：被拆掉的是颜色与不需要的化合物，而不是金属被消耗。

intro.en: Oxidize is built on oxide, itself from oxygen, the French scientific name of 1777; the verb's first date is approximate.
intro.cn: oxidize 由 oxide 派生，而 oxide 又出自 oxygen 这一 1777 年的法语科学命名；该动词的首见年代为约数。

items.en: The name of oxygen joins Greek oxys 'sharp, acid' with -genes 'producing', because Lavoisier believed the gas was required for acids.
items.cn: 氧的名称把希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」与 -genes「产生」合在一起，因为拉瓦锡相信酸的形成需要这种气体。

items.en: Lavoisier's new name spread through European science, and English adopted it at the end of the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 拉瓦锡的新名称在欧洲科学界传开，英语于 18 世纪末采用。

items.en: A compound of an element with oxygen was called an oxide, formed on the model of the new gas name with a chemical noun ending.
items.cn: 元素与氧形成的化合物被称为 oxide，是按新气体名称配上化学名词词尾构成的。

items.en: Oxidize was built directly on oxide with the ordinary verb ending that means 'to make or become', parallel to many other chemical verbs.
items.cn: oxidize 直接在 oxide 上加表示「使成为、变成」的普通动词词尾构成，与许多其他化学动词同型。

items.en: As chemistry, medicine and industry expanded, the verb was applied to metals, food, fuels, dyes and living tissue, and the noun oxidation followed the same range.
items.cn: 随着化学、医学与工业扩张，这个动词被用于金属、食物、燃料、染料与活组织，名词 oxidation 也覆盖同样的范围。

items.en: First date uncertain: the verb is recorded from the turn of the nineteenth century, but the earliest citations for the wider electron sense belong to later decades and are not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：该动词在 19 世纪之交已有记录，但更宽的失电子义的最早引文要晚数十年，具体年份并未精确固定。

note.en: The first group shares the oxygen stem and differs by word class; the second group holds the paired or neighbouring changes in the same reaction.
note.cn: 第一组共享由氧派生的词干而词类不同；第二组是同一反应中与之配对或相邻的变化。

entries.definition: The event itself; the verb names what an agent does, while the noun names what happens.
entries.definitionCN: 事件本身；动词命名作用者所做的事，名词命名所发生的事。

entries.definition: The compound left behind; it cannot take an object and describes no change in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 留下的化合物；它不能带宾语，也不描述进行中的变化。

entries.definition: A participle or adjective for matter that has already changed, not for the act of changing it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示已经变化的物质的分词或形容词，而不是使其变化的动作。

entries.definition: The substance that accepts electrons and drives the change; in everyday writing oxidizer is the more common twin.
entries.definitionCN: 接受电子并推动变化的物质；日常写作中更常见的是 oxidizer 这一同义形式。

entries.definition: To add electrons or lower an oxidation number; every oxidation is balanced by a reduction somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 加上电子或降低氧化数；每一处氧化都在别处由还原平衡。

entries.definition: To wear a metal away by chemical action; it describes the damage rather than the electron transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 借化学作用磨损金属；它描述损坏，而非电子转移。

entries.definition: To dull or discolour a metal surface, especially silver; it is a visible result of oxidation, not its general name.
entries.definitionCN: 使金属表面失去光泽或变色，尤指银；它是氧化的可见结果，而非其通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oxide plus the verb ending: to turn something into an oxide.
normal.cn: oxide 加动词词尾：把某物变成氧化物。

normal.en: The family runs oxide, oxidize, oxidation, oxidized, oxidizing, oxidizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oxide、oxidize、oxidation、oxidized、oxidizing、oxidizer。

normal.en: Typical objects: oxidize a metal, oxidize fats, oxidize the surface.
normal.cn: 典型宾语：使金属氧化、使脂肪氧化、氧化表面。

normal.en: Air does it slowly, a reagent does it fast, a cell does it for energy.
normal.cn: 空气做得慢，试剂做得快，细胞则为了取能而做。

normal.en: The same verb can ruin a nail or protect an aluminium panel.
normal.cn: 同一个动词既能让钉子报废，也能保护铝板。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of apple browning on a plate before anyone touches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片苹果摆在盘子里，没人碰就先变褐。

abstract.en: Picture a silver spoon going grey in the drawer where it is never used.
abstract.cn: 想象一把银勺在抽屉里久不使用，慢慢变灰。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed bottle that slowly loses its sparkle because air got in.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶密封饮料因为进了空气，慢慢失去气泡感。

examples.en: Heat and light oxidize the pigment, so the sign fades.
examples.cn: 热与光会氧化颜料，于是标牌褪色。

examples.en: The alloy oxidizes more slowly than pure iron.
examples.cn: 这种合金比纯铁氧化得慢。

examples.en: Bacteria oxidize the sulfides in the sediment.
examples.cn: 细菌氧化沉积物中的硫化物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oxi（氧）+ dize（使）」——让氧上身，就是使氧化

root: 英语 oxide（出自 oxygen，1777 年法语科学命名，取自希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」+ -genes「产生」）+ 动词词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one transfer of electrons: oxygen joins, charge leaves, a surface rusts, food spoils, cells burn fuel, an element climbs in valence, a protective film grows, and a dye is bleached away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次电子转移：氧结合进来、电荷离开、表面生锈、食物变陈、细胞烧燃料、元素价态上升、保护膜生成、染料被漂掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail under a leaking roof, its bright skin turning into a soft orange powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：漏雨棚下的铁钉，亮皮变成松软的橘色粉末。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY READING: air alone makes a metal combine with oxygen, and the result is plain rust or tarnish.
branches.cn: 日常读法：仅靠空气就让金属与氧结合，结果就是直白的锈或暗斑。

branches.en: THE CHEMIST'S READING: electrons are pushed out and an element is driven to a higher valence.
branches.cn: 化学家的读法：电子被推走，某元素被推上更高的价态。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN COST: air attacks a flavour instead of a surface, and the change is tasted rather than seen.
branches.cn: 厨房的代价：空气攻击的是味道而非表面，变化靠尝而非靠看。

branches.en: THE ENERGY USE: cells oxidize fuel on purpose because the transfer releases power.
branches.cn: 能量的用法：细胞有意氧化燃料，因为这一转移能放出能量。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL TWIST: the same reaction is made to seal a panel or to strip colour from cloth.
branches.cn: 工业的转折：同一反应被用来封住板材，或被用来剥去布上的颜色。

intro.en: Oxidize is a stem from the name of oxygen with a verb ending, and the family keeps that stem in every form.
intro.cn: oxidize 是以氧的名称作词干、再加动词词尾构成，整个词族在各种形式里都保留这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Greek and passed through French scientific naming; Latin supplies only the endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干源自希腊语并经法语科学命名传入；拉丁语只提供词尾，因此不列出该词根的拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 开头的成分指向「产酸」这一说法。

items.example: The suffix says the gas produces the quality named first.
items.exampleCN: 后缀说明这种气体产生前面所指的性质。

items.example: Oxidation is faster in wet air.
items.exampleCN: 湿空气中氧化更快。

items.example: The oxidized surface no longer shines.
items.exampleCN: 已氧化的表面不再发亮。

items.example: Nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent.
items.exampleCN: 硝酸是强氧化剂。

items.example: The fuel needs an oxidizer to burn in space.
items.exampleCN: 燃料在太空燃烧需要氧化剂。

senses.title: Make smaller in size or amount
senses.titleCN: 在大小或数量上使之变小
senses.definition: to make something smaller, fewer or less in amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在体积、数量或总量上变小变少
senses.example: Insulation reduces heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿墙而走的热量。
senses.why: The core gesture is bringing something down; the modern everyday sense simply applies that downward motion to quantity and size.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是「把某物带下来」；现代日常义只是把这个向下的动作用在数量与大小上。

senses.title: Lower a price, rate or level
senses.definition: to bring a price, rate, speed or level down to a lower figure
senses.definitionCN: 把价格、比率、速度或水平降到一个更低的数值
senses.example: The store reduced prices by a fifth before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 节前商店把价格降了五分之一。
senses.why: Prices and rates are quantities on a scale, so the same downward gesture is read as a movement along that scale.
senses.whyCN: 价格与比率是尺度上的量，因此同一个向下动作被读作沿尺度向下移动。

senses.title: Bring a problem to a simpler form
senses.titleCN: 把问题归结为更简单的形式
senses.definition: to restate a complicated thing as a simpler one that explains it
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂之事重新表述为能解释它的更简单之事
senses.example: The authors reduce the argument to a single question.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把这个论证归结为一个问题。
senses.why: A simpler form carries the same content in fewer parts, so reduction here means stripping away what can be dropped.
senses.whyCN: 更简单的形式用更少的部件承载同样的内容，因此这里的「减」指剥掉可以舍去的部分。

senses.title: Force into a worse condition
senses.definition: to bring someone or something into a lower or worse state, often with 'to'
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物带到更低、更糟的状态，常与表示「到」的介词连用
senses.example: The flood reduced the village to a few broken walls.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水使村庄只剩几堵断墙。
senses.why: The downward movement can be read as loss of standing, so the verb also describes being brought low rather than made smaller.
senses.whyCN: 向下的移动也可以读作地位的丧失，于是这个动词也描述「被压低」，而不是「被缩小」。

senses.title: Simplify a fraction in arithmetic
senses.definition: to divide the top and bottom of a fraction by a common number so that the value stays the same but the figures get smaller
senses.definitionCN: 用公因数同时除分子与分母，使数值不变而数字变小
senses.example: Students reduce the fraction before adding it to another.
senses.exampleCN: 学生先把分数约分，再与另一个分数相加。
senses.why: Arithmetic keeps the value while shrinking the written figures, which is the clearest small-scale model of the whole word.
senses.whyCN: 算术让数值保持不变而让写出的数字变小，这是整个词最小尺度、也最清晰的模型。

senses.title: Boil a liquid down
senses.definition: to cook a liquid until it thickens and its volume falls
senses.definitionCN: 加热液体使其变稠、体积减少
senses.example: Long simmering will reduce the sauce to a thick glaze.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间小火慢熬会把酱汁收成浓稠的亮汁。
senses.why: Cooking turns the abstract downward movement into something visible: steam leaves and what remains is denser.
senses.whyCN: 烹调把这个抽象的向下运动变成可见之事：水汽走掉，剩下的更浓。

senses.title: Add electrons in chemistry
senses.definition: to add electrons to an atom, ion or molecule, or to remove oxygen from it
senses.definitionCN: 给原子、离子或分子加上电子，或从中去掉氧
senses.example: Carbon can reduce the metal oxide to the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 碳能把金属氧化物还原成金属。
senses.why: The chemical sense came from the older notion of bringing a substance back to a simpler state: the ore returns to bare metal.
senses.whyCN: 化学义来自更早的「把物质带回更简单的状态」：矿石退回为纯金属。

senses.title: Put a bone or joint back in place
senses.definition: to restore a displaced bone or joint to its proper position
senses.definitionCN: 把错位的骨头或关节恢复到正确位置
senses.example: The doctor reduced the shoulder and strapped the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 医生使肩关节复位，并把手臂固定好。
senses.why: Medicine uses the original 'bring back' reading literally: the part is led back to where it belongs.
senses.whyCN: 医学把最初「带回」的读法用在字面上：那个部位被领回原位。

senses.title: Sum up raw data
senses.titleCN: 把原始数据归纳成摘要
senses.definition: to turn a set of measurements into a few summary figures
senses.definitionCN: 把一组测量值变成少数几个汇总数字
senses.example: The software reduces thousands of readings to a mean and a range.
senses.exampleCN: 软件把上千个读数归纳成一个均值与一个范围。
senses.why: Statistics repeats the simplifying gesture: many pieces become one figure that is easier to hold.
senses.whyCN: 统计学重复了那个简化动作：许多碎片变成一个更易把握的数字。

intro.en: Reduce comes from Latin reducere, 'to lead back', built on re- 'back' and ducere 'to lead'. English shortened the sense to 'bring down' and later added technical uses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reduce 来自拉丁 reducere「领回」，由 re-「向后」与 ducere「引领」构成；英语把词义收窄到「使降低」，之后又长出各种专门用法。年代为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead or draw along', the root behind duke, duct and conduct; the idea is direction rather than shrinking.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引领、牵引」，是 duke、duct、conduct 等词背后的词根；其核心是方向，而不是缩小。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus ducere produced reducere, 'to lead back, bring back, restore', as one brings a traveller or a troop home.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 ducere 构成 reducere「领回、带回、恢复」，如同把旅人或队伍带回家。

items.en: English took the word through Old French, first in the senses of bringing back, restoring and leading a person to a place.
items.cn: 英语经古法语引入该词，最初指带回、恢复、把人领到某处。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the verb increasingly meant bringing something to a lower figure or condition, and that reading now dominates ordinary use.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪起，这个动词越来越多地指把某物带到更低的数值或状态，这一读法如今在日常用法中占主导。

items.en: Cooking added the simmering sense, arithmetic the simplifying of fractions, and medicine the restoring of a joint; chemistry adopted 'reduce' for the removal of oxygen, later generalised to the gain of electrons.
items.cn: 烹调加上收汁义，算术加上约分义，医学加上关节复位义；化学用这个词指去掉氧，后来又一般化为「获得电子」。

items.en: First date uncertain for the sense shift: the date at which the 'lessen' sense overtook the older 'bring back' sense is inferred from citation records, not a fixed event.
items.cn: 义项转变的首见年代不确定：表示「减少」的义项何时压过更早的「带回」义，是根据文献记录作出的推断，并非某一个确定事件。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root and is constantly confused; the second group holds other words for making something less.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根，极易混淆；第二组是其他表示「使变少」的词。

entries.tag: the noun of the same verb
entries.definition: The act or result of reducing, including the chemical gain of electrons; it names the event, not the action of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 减少的动作或结果，也包括化学上的获得电子；它命名事件，而非执行动作。

entries.definition: Built on de- 'down from' plus ducere: to draw a conclusion out of given premises, which is reasoning, not shrinking.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-「从……向下」加 ducere 构成：从给定前提出结论，属推理，不属缩小。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus ducere: to lead someone into a state or to bring about an effect, with no sense of lessening.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 ducere：把某人引入某种状态或促成某结果，与「变少」无关。

entries.definition: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere: to bring something out into existence; the root is shared but the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「向前」加 ducere：把某物带出来使其存在；词根相同但方向相反。

entries.definition: To become or make less in number or size; it states the change of amount without the idea of simplifying or restoring.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或大小上变少或使之变少；它只说量的变化，不含简化或恢复之意。

entries.definition: To move something down in height, level or rank; it suits a position on a scale better than a bulk of material.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物在高度、水平或等级上往下移；它更适合尺度上的位置，而非成堆的物质。

entries.definition: To remove a portion, especially of cost, text or supply; it stresses the removal rather than the resulting smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉一部分，尤指费用、文字或供应；它强调移除，而非变小后的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus ducere 'lead': the oldest picture is leading something back home.
normal.cn: re-「向后」加 ducere「引领」：最早的画面是把某物领回家。

normal.en: The family runs reduce, reduction, reduced, reducing, reducible, reducer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reduce、reduction、reduced、reducing、reducible、reducer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern sense: reduce costs, reduce the risk, reduce emissions.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代义：降低成本、降低风险、减少排放。

normal.en: The same root leads in deduce, induce and produce, each with a different direction.
normal.cn: 同一词根也出现在 deduce、induce 与 produce 中，各自的方向不同。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps an old picture: ore is led back to bare metal.
normal.cn: 化学保留了一个旧画面：矿石被领回成纯金属。

abstract.en: Picture a wide pot of soup losing its steam until only a spoonful of glaze is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一大锅汤不断散走水汽，最后只剩一勺浓汁。

abstract.en: Picture a long report folded again and again until one small square remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一份长报告被反复对折，最后只剩一个小方块。

abstract.en: Picture a scattered crowd walking back through one gate until the field is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象散开的人群从一道门走回，最后场地空了。

examples.en: Better lamps reduce the electricity bill in winter.
examples.cn: 更好的灯具能降低冬季电费。

examples.en: The committee reduced the proposal to three short points.
examples.cn: 委员会把提案归结为三条短要点。

examples.en: Hydrogen can reduce the oxide at high temperature.
examples.cn: 氢在高温下能还原这种氧化物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ duce（引导）」——把数量往回领，就是减少

root: 拉丁 reducere「领回、带回」= re-（向后）+ ducere「引领」；英语先取「带回、恢复」义，后转为「使降低、减少」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one downward or backward gesture: quantity falls, price falls, a problem is simplified, a person is brought low, a fraction shrinks, a sauce thickens, an ore returns to metal, a joint returns to place, and data is folded into a summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个向下或向回的动作：数量下降、价格下降、问题被简化、人被压低、分数变小、酱汁变浓、矿石退回金属、关节回到原位、数据被折成摘要。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide pot of sauce simmering down to a spoonful of thick glaze.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口宽锅里的酱汁慢慢收成一勺浓汁。

branches.en: DOWN THE SCALE: whatever is counted or priced moves to a smaller figure, from heat loss to holiday prices.
branches.cn: 沿尺度向下：凡可计数或标价之物都移向更小的数字，从热损失到节日价格。

branches.en: FEWER PARTS: an argument or a pile of readings is restated in a form that can be held at once.
branches.cn: 更少的部件：论证或一堆读数被重新表述成可以一次握住的形式。

branches.en: LED TO A PLACE: a village is led down to rubble, and a shoulder is led back into its socket.
branches.cn: 被领到某处：村庄被带到只剩瓦砾，肩关节被领回关节窝。

branches.en: SHRINKING THE WRITTEN OR THE LIQUID: a fraction loses common factors, a sauce loses water.
branches.cn: 缩小写下的或流动的：分数失去公因数，酱汁失去水分。

branches.en: THE ORE RETURNS: chemistry keeps the oldest picture and calls the gain of electrons a leading back.
branches.cn: 矿石退回：化学保留最古老的画面，把获得电子称为「领回」。

intro.en: Reduce is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb root, and both parts are unusually productive in English.
intro.cn: reduce 由一个拉丁前缀加一个拉丁动词词根构成，这两部分在英语里都异常能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives duct, conduct, induce, produce and deduce, while re- recur in return, remain and reflect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 duct、conduct、induce、produce 与 deduce，而 re- 也反复出现在 return、remain 与 reflect 中。

items.example: The prefix supplies the backward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供向后的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供牵引的动作。

items.meaning: to lead back; to bring down
items.example: The verb still carries a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词至今带着方向感。

items.structure: reduce plus the action noun ending
items.meaning: the act or result of reducing
items.example: The reduction in cost was welcome.
items.exampleCN: 成本的降低很受欢迎。

items.example: The reduced price applies at weekends.
items.exampleCN: 优惠价在周末适用。

items.meaning: causing a decrease; chemically able to add electrons
items.meaningCN: 起减少作用的；化学上能提供电子的
items.example: A reducing agent gives electrons away.
items.exampleCN: 还原剂把电子让出去。

items.structure: reduce plus the 'able to be' ending
items.example: The fraction is reducible by three.
items.exampleCN: 这个分数可以用三约分。

items.meaning: a substance or device that reduces
items.example: A reducer joins pipes of different widths.
items.exampleCN: 异径接头把不同粗细的管子接起来。

latinEntries.structure: ducere, duco, duxi, ductum (v., third conjugation)

derivatives.zh: 由 reduce 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「减少；还原」
由 reduce 加已然词尾构成，义为「已减少的；已还原的」
由 reduce 加进行词尾构成，义为「有还原能力的」
由 reduce 加「能够被……的」后缀构成，义为「可减少的；可约分的」
由 reduce 加施动词尾构成，义为「还原剂；缩小装置」

definition_zh: 氧化还原；氧化还原反应（电子在物质间转移的一对过程）
definition_en: the paired processes of oxidation and reduction, treated as one reaction in which electrons move from one substance to another
core_image: 两个相连的槽里，一边的金属失去电子、慢慢溶开，另一边的离子接过电子、沉成亮片
scene: 水处理池底部，一边的铁屑慢慢溶掉，另一边的金属离子接过电子沉成薄片。Redox in the tank decides whether the metal stays dissolved or settles as a solid.
sceneCN: 这里 redox 指氧化与还原成对发生的电子转移过程（第 1 个义项：氧化还原的统称）；句意：池中的氧化还原条件决定该金属是继续溶解还是沉成固体。图中可辨识物件：水处理池、铁屑、析出的薄片、流动的水。

pos.zh: 氧化还原；氧化还原反应
氧化还原的（多作定语，如氧化还原电位）

derivatives.zh: 由 redox 加表示「具有……活性」的复合成分构成，义为「具氧化还原活性的」
由 redox 加表示「与……耦合」的复合成分构成，义为「与氧化还原相耦合的」

senses.title: Oxidation and reduction as one event
senses.titleCN: 氧化与还原作为同一个事件
senses.definition: the combined process in which one substance is oxidized while another is reduced, because electrons cannot simply vanish
senses.definitionCN: 一种物质被氧化、另一种被还原的合并过程，因为电子不可能凭空消失
senses.example: Redox in the tank decides whether the metal stays dissolved or settles as a solid.
senses.exampleCN: 池中的氧化还原条件决定该金属是继续溶解还是沉成固体。
senses.why: The word is a blend of reduction and oxidation, so it names the two halves as a single transaction rather than two separate events.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「还原」与「氧化」两个词的缩合，因此它把两半当作一笔交易，而不是两件分开的事。

senses.title: Electrons moving between substances
senses.definition: the transfer of electrons from a donor to an acceptor during a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 反应中电子从供体转移到受体
senses.example: The redox step moves two electrons from iron to oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 这一步氧化还原把两个电子从铁移给氧。
senses.why: Once both halves are defined by electron bookkeeping, the joint word naturally describes the movement of those electrons.
senses.whyCN: 当两半都用电子记账来定义之后，这个合并词自然就描述这些电子的移动。

senses.title: A matched pair of chemical forms
senses.definition: a pair consisting of a substance and its oxidized or reduced counterpart, which can interconvert by electron transfer
senses.definitionCN: 由某物质与其氧化或还原对应物组成的成对体系，可通过电子转移互相转换
senses.example: The two forms make a redox couple that buffers the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种形态构成一个氧化还原对，为溶液提供缓冲。
senses.why: If every oxidation needs a reduction, the reacting substances come in pairs, and the pair itself becomes a named unit.
senses.whyCN: 既然每次氧化都需要一次还原，参与反应的物质就以成对形式出现，这一对本身也成了一个被命名的单位。

senses.title: The voltage of that pair
senses.definition: the electrical potential that measures how strongly a redox couple tends to accept or give up electrons
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一个氧化还原对接受或让出电子倾向强弱的电势
senses.example: A higher redox potential favours the oxidized form.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的氧化还原电位有利于氧化形态。
senses.why: The pull between the two halves can be measured as a voltage, so the abstract pair acquires a number.
senses.whyCN: 两半之间的拉扯可以被量成电压，于是抽象的一对有了一个数字。

senses.title: The balance inside a living cell
senses.titleCN: 活细胞内部的氧化还原平衡
senses.definition: the internal balance between oxidizing and reducing conditions that keeps metabolism working
senses.definitionCN: 细胞内氧化性条件与还原性条件之间的平衡，维持代谢运转
senses.example: The cell keeps its redox state stable under stress.
senses.exampleCN: 受压时细胞仍维持其氧化还原状态稳定。
senses.why: Cells run both halves constantly, so the joint word names a standing condition rather than a single reaction.
senses.whyCN: 细胞同时不断运行两半，因此这个合并词命名一种持续状态，而不是单次反应。

senses.title: Conditions in soil, sediment or water
senses.titleCN: 土壤、沉积物或水中的条件
senses.definition: the prevailing oxidizing or reducing character of an environment, which controls which minerals and metals remain stable
senses.definitionCN: 环境整体的氧化性或还原性特征，决定哪些矿物与金属能稳定存在
senses.example: Buried sediment quickly becomes reducing, and its redox shifts with depth.
senses.exampleCN: 埋藏的沉积物很快转为还原性，其氧化还原状态随深度改变。
senses.why: Environmental science scales the pair up from a beaker to a whole layer of mud or water, where it acts as a setting.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把这一对从烧杯放大到整层泥或水，在那里它成了背景条件。

senses.title: A titration based on electron transfer
senses.titleCN: 以电子转移为基础的滴定
senses.definition: a laboratory procedure that measures concentration by adding a reagent until a redox couple changes state
senses.definitionCN: 通过加入试剂直到氧化还原对改变状态来测定浓度的实验方法
senses.example: The redox titration turned the solution pink at the end point.
senses.exampleCN: 氧化还原滴定在终点使溶液变成粉红。
senses.why: Because the pair changes visibly at a definite point, it can be used as a measuring device.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一对在某一点会明显变色，它可以被当作测量装置使用。

senses.title: The balanced equation of the pair
senses.titleCN: 成对过程的配平方程式
senses.definition: the written form in which the electrons lost and gained are counted out so that both halves balance
senses.definitionCN: 把失去与得到的电子逐一点清、使两半相互配平的书写形式
senses.example: Students balance the redox equation before calculating the yield.
senses.exampleCN: 学生先配平氧化还原方程式，再计算产率。
senses.why: Since the two halves must balance exactly, the joint word also names the exercise of writing them as one balanced statement.
senses.whyCN: 由于两半必须严格配平，这个合并词也指把它们写成一个配平式子的练习。

intro.en: Redox is a twentieth-century blend of reduction and oxidation, two words with separate histories. The exact first citation is uncertain.
intro.cn: redox 是 20 世纪由 reduction 与 oxidation 缩合而成的新词，而这两个词各有独立的历史；确切的最早引文年代不确定。

items.en: Reduction goes back to Latin reducere 'to lead back'; chemistry borrowed the word for driving oxygen out of a substance, and later for adding electrons.
items.cn: reduction 可上溯到拉丁 reducere「领回」；化学借它指把氧从物质中赶走，后来又指加上电子。

items.en: Oxidation goes back to oxygen, the French name of 1777 built from Greek words for 'sharp' and 'producing'.
items.cn: oxidation 可上溯到 1777 年的法语名称 oxygen，该名称由希腊语表示「尖锐」与「产生」的词构成。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry established that the two changes always occur together, since electrons lost by one substance are gained by another.
items.cn: 19 世纪化学确立了两者总是同时发生：一种物质失去的电子必被另一种物质得到。

items.en: The shortened blend redox appeared in the early twentieth century, when electrochemistry and biochemistry needed a single handy word for the paired process.
items.cn: 缩合形式 redox 出现在 20 世纪早期，当时电化学与生物化学需要一个顺手的单词来指这一成对过程。

items.en: The term spread from the laboratory to soil science, water treatment, corrosion studies and cell biology, always keeping the sense of a matched pair.
items.cn: 这个术语从实验室扩展到土壤学、水处理、腐蚀研究与细胞生物学，始终保留「成对」的意思。

items.en: First date uncertain: the blend is usually dated to the early twentieth century, but the earliest printed citation is not securely fixed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个缩合词通常被定在 20 世纪早期，但最早的印刷引文未被确凿固定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like redox and names its parts; the second group names processes that are easily mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 redox 相近，且命名其组成部分；第二组是容易被误当成它的过程。

entries.definition: The gain of electrons or loss of oxygen, one of the two halves that the blend joins together.
entries.definitionCN: 获得电子或失去氧，是缩合词所合并的两半之一。

entries.definition: The loss of electrons or gain of oxygen, the partner that always accompanies reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 失去电子或获得氧，总是与还原相伴的那一半。

entries.definition: The measured voltage of a redox couple; here redox is a modifier, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 某一氧化还原对测得的电压；这里 redox 是修饰成分，不是整个过程。

entries.definition: The matched pair of oxidized and reduced forms that a redox reaction interconverts.
entries.definitionCN: 氧化形态与还原形态组成的成对体系，氧化还原反应使二者互相转换。

entries.definition: The physical movement of electrons from one species to another; redox is the chemical name for the whole paired event.
entries.definitionCN: 电子从一个物种移到另一个物种的物理运动；redox 是这整件成对事件的化学名称。

entries.definition: The branch of chemistry that studies reactions involving electron flow; redox reactions are its central objects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究涉及电子流动的反应的化学分支；氧化还原反应是其核心对象。

entries.definition: The wearing away of metal by its surroundings, usually a redox reaction in disguise; the word names the damage, not the chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 金属被周围环境磨损，通常是伪装的氧化还原反应；这个词命名损坏，而非化学过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is a blend of the opening of reduction and the ending of oxidation.
normal.cn: 这个词把 reduction 的开头与 oxidation 的结尾缩合在一起。

normal.en: The paired idea is exact: electrons lost by one substance are gained by another.
normal.cn: 成对的意思很精确：一种物质失去的电子被另一种物质得到。

normal.en: Fixed terms show the measured side: redox potential, redox couple, redox titration.
normal.cn: 固定术语显示可测量的一面：氧化还原电位、氧化还原对、氧化还原滴定。

normal.en: Cells keep a redox state, soil has redox conditions, tanks run redox reactions.
normal.cn: 细胞维持氧化还原状态，土壤有氧化还原条件，水池里发生氧化还原反应。

normal.en: The two halves are never separate: there is no oxidation without a reduction somewhere.
normal.cn: 两半从不分开：任何氧化都必在别处有相应的还原。

abstract.en: Picture two hands passing a coin back and forth, so neither hand is ever empty for long.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手来回传递一枚硬币，两只手都不会长久空着。

abstract.en: Picture a seesaw where one side can rise only because the other side goes down.
abstract.cn: 想象一架跷跷板，一边能升起来只因为另一边落下去。

abstract.en: Picture two banks settling a debt by moving the same sum in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两家银行通过同一笔款项朝相反方向划转来结清债务。

examples.en: The battery stores energy in a reversible redox reaction.
examples.cn: 电池把能量储存在可逆的氧化还原反应里。

examples.en: Scientists measured the redox potential of the groundwater.
examples.cn: 科学家测量了地下水的氧化还原电位。

examples.en: Balancing a redox equation means counting electrons on both sides.
examples.cn: 配平氧化还原方程式意味着把两边的电子数都点清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reduction 的头 + oxidation 的尾」——氧化与还原合成一个词

root: 英语 reduction（拉丁 reducere「领回」）与 oxidation（oxygen，1777 年法语命名）的缩合；首见年代约在 20 世纪早期，确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one paired exchange: the two halves as a single event, the electrons that move, the matched pair of forms, the voltage of that pair, a cell's standing balance, an environment's conditions, a titration, and a balanced equation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次成对交换：两半合成一个事件、移动的电子、成对的形态、这一对的电压、细胞的常态平衡、环境的条件、一次滴定、一个配平式子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one trough losing metal while the other trough grows bright flakes from the same electrons.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个槽里的金属在减少，另一个槽里用同一批电子长出亮片。

branches.en: THE SINGLE TRANSACTION: the blend names both halves at once, and what links them is the electrons in transit.
branches.cn: 单笔交易：这个缩合词一次命名两半，而连接它们的是行进中的电子。

branches.en: THE PAIR AND ITS PULL: the two forms constitute a unit, and the strength of their pull is read as a voltage.
branches.cn: 这一对及其拉扯：两种形态构成一个单位，拉扯的强弱被读成电压。

branches.en: THE STANDING CONDITION: in a cell the exchange never stops, so the pair becomes a steady internal state.
branches.cn: 持续状态：在细胞里交换从不停歇，于是这一对变成稳定的内部状态。

branches.en: THE SETTING AND THE INSTRUMENT: a layer of mud has a redox character, and a titration turns that character into a reading.
branches.cn: 背景与仪器：一层泥有其氧化还原性格，而滴定把这种性格变成一个读数。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN FORM: the two halves are counted out until the equation balances.
branches.cn: 书写形式：两半被逐一点清，直到方程式配平。

intro.en: Redox is not built from living affixes but cut from two existing words, so its parts are the two chemical names it joins.
intro.cn: redox 不是由现成活用的词缀构成，而是从两个已有单词剪接而来，因此它的部件就是它所合并的两个化学名称。

latinIntro.en: The two source words reach Latin separately, one through reducere and one through the French name for oxygen, so they are not a single Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 两个来源词各自上溯到拉丁语，一个经 reducere，一个经法语中的氧名称，因此它们并不构成同一个拉丁词族。

items.example: The first fragment carries the reducing half of the pair.
items.exampleCN: 开头这一截承载这一对中的还原部分。

items.example: The second fragment carries the oxidizing half.
items.exampleCN: 后面这一截承载氧化部分。

items.structure: blend of the two chemical nouns
items.example: The blend names one transaction, not two.
items.exampleCN: 这个缩合词命名一笔交易，而不是两笔。

items.structure: redox plus the general reaction noun
items.meaning: a reaction of the paired kind
items.example: A redox reaction moves electrons between species.
items.exampleCN: 氧化还原反应在物种之间转移电子。

items.structure: redox plus the noun for electrical potential
items.example: The redox potential tells which side pulls harder.
items.exampleCN: 氧化还原电位说明哪一边拉得更紧。

items.structure: redox plus the noun for a matched pair
items.example: The redox couple buffers the solution.
items.exampleCN: 这个氧化还原对为溶液提供缓冲。

items.structure: redox plus the noun for condition
items.example: Stress alters the redox state of the cell.
items.exampleCN: 压力会改变细胞的氧化还原状态。

items.structure: redox plus the noun for a measured addition
items.example: The redox titration reached a sharp end point.
items.exampleCN: 氧化还原滴定到达了鲜明的终点。

derivatives.zh: 由 redox 加表示「具有……活性」的复合成分构成，义为「具氧化还原活性的」
由 redox 加表示「与……耦合」的复合成分构成，义为「与氧化还原相耦合的」

definition_zh: 酸；酸性物质；酸味的；尖刻的；（俚）迷幻药
definition_en: a substance that reacts with a base and can donate protons, or the sharp sour quality such a substance has
core_image: 一只木桶里装着浅色液体，凑近一闻鼻子里发紧，舌尖也跟着缩起来
scene: 醋坊的桶盖一揭开，气味还没到鼻子，舌头先被那股尖利的味道刺得缩起来。Acid in the vat bites the tongue before the smell even reaches you.
sceneCN: 这里 acid 指能给出质子、带强烈酸味的物质（第 1 个义项：酸这一化学物质）；句意：桶里的酸在气味抵达之前就先刺得舌头缩起。图中可辨识物件：木桶、浅色液体、盖板、被酸味刺激的表情。

forms.label: 比较级（更酸的；更尖刻的）
最高级（最酸的；最尖刻的）

derivatives.zh: 由 acid 加表示「具有……性质」的形容词后缀构成，义为「酸性的」
由 acid 加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「酸性；酸度」
由 acid 加表示「使成为」的动词后缀构成，义为「使变酸」
由 acidify 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「酸化过程」

senses.title: A chemical that reacts with a base
senses.titleCN: 与碱起反应的化学物质
senses.definition: a substance that can donate protons or accept electron pairs, and reacts with a base to form a salt
senses.definitionCN: 能给出质子或接受电子对、并与碱反应生成盐的物质
senses.example: Acid in the vat bites the tongue before the smell even reaches you.
senses.exampleCN: 桶里的酸在气味抵达之前就先刺得舌头缩起。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the sour substance itself, and the modern chemical definition keeps that name for the class of things that taste sharp and attack bases.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是这种酸味物质本身，现代化学定义把这个名称保留给一类尝起来尖利、会侵蚀碱的东西。

senses.title: A sour liquid in the kitchen
senses.definition: a sour liquid used in cooking or preserving, such as vinegar or lemon juice
senses.definitionCN: 用于烹调或腌渍的酸味液体，如醋或柠檬汁
senses.example: A drop of acid lifts the flavour of the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴酸味液体就能提亮汤的味道。
senses.why: Cooks meet the chemical class in bottles and fruit, so the same noun covers the everyday sour ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 厨师是在瓶子和水果里遇到这一类化学物质的，因此同一个名词也覆盖日常的酸味食材。

senses.title: The taste of sharp sourness
senses.definition: the sharp, mouth-tightening quality that sour things have
senses.definitionCN: 酸物所带的、使口腔收紧的尖利性质
senses.example: The unripe plum has a clean acid bite.
senses.exampleCN: 未熟的梅子有一种清亮的酸劲。
senses.why: The noun shifted into an adjective-like use because the quality and the substance were felt as one thing at the table.
senses.whyCN: 名词向形容词性用法滑动，因为在餐桌上，这种性质与这种物质被感受为同一件事。

senses.title: A cutting remark
senses.definition: words that are deliberately sharp, bitter or wounding
senses.definitionCN: 有意尖利、刻薄或伤人的话
senses.example: His acid comment ended the meeting early.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句尖刻的话让会议提前结束。
senses.why: A sharp taste and a sharp tongue share the same bodily image: both make the listener wince.
senses.whyCN: 尖利的味道与尖利的舌头共享同一个身体感受：都会让听者皱眉缩舌。

senses.title: Rain made sour by pollution
senses.definition: rain or snow that has become acidic after absorbing industrial gases
senses.definitionCN: 吸收工业气体后变酸的雨或雪
senses.example: Acid rain has stripped the leaves from the hillside trees.
senses.exampleCN: 酸雨把山坡树上的叶子剥光了。
senses.why: Environmental writing attaches the substance to weather, because the acid is carried in the water rather than held in a container.
senses.whyCN: 环境写作把这种物质与天气连在一起，因为酸是被水带走的，而不是装在一个容器里。

senses.title: The decisive test
senses.definition: a test that proves whether something is genuine or good enough
senses.definitionCN: 用来证明某物是否真实或足够好的检验
senses.example: The acid test of a plan is whether it survives a budget cut.
senses.exampleCN: 检验一个计划的关键，是看它能否在预算削减后存活。
senses.why: The phrase comes from the old use of acid to test gold, so a sharp reagent that reveals what a metal really is became a picture of any decisive proof.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法来自旧时用酸检验黄金的做法：能揭出金属真面目的尖利试剂，成了任何决定性证明的图景。

senses.title: Acid used to etch or clean
senses.definition: a strong acid applied to metal, glass or stone to cut, clean or dull a surface
senses.definitionCN: 施于金属、玻璃或石材以切割、清洗或使表面变哑的强酸
senses.example: The workshop uses acid to etch the pattern into the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 作坊用酸把图案蚀刻进版面上。
senses.why: Industry turns the substance into a tool, and the noun names the agent of a deliberate surface change.
senses.whyCN: 工业把这种物质变成工具，名词于是命名一个有意改变表面的作用者。

senses.title: The lab name for a proton donor
senses.titleCN: 实验室里「质子给体」的称呼
senses.definition: in modern chemical language, any species that gives up a proton to another species
senses.definitionCN: 现代化学用语中，把质子让给另一物种的任何物种
senses.example: Every proton donor in the beaker counts as an acid.
senses.exampleCN: 烧杯里每一个给出质子的物种都算作酸。
senses.why: The definition widened from sour liquids to any proton donor, and the old noun was kept for the whole class.
senses.whyCN: 定义从酸味液体扩展到任何质子给体，而旧名词被保留下来指整个类别。

senses.title: Street slang for a drug
senses.titleCN: 指某种药物的街头俚语
senses.definition: a slang name for lysergic acid diethylamide, used mainly in the middle decades of the twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 麦角酸二乙酰胺的俚语叫法，主要用于 20 世纪中叶数十年
senses.example: The old posters warn about acid in the dance halls.
senses.exampleCN: 旧海报警告舞厅里出现的迷幻药。
senses.why: The slang borrows the chemical noun for a drug whose full name contains the word, so the short form became the street name.
senses.whyCN: 这一俚语借用这个化学名词来指某种药，因为其全名里含有该词，简称就成了街头叫法。

intro.en: Acid came through Old French from Latin acidus 'sour', a word for taste that chemistry later turned into a class name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: acid 经古法语来自拉丁 acidus「酸的」，本是一个表示味道的词，化学后来把它变成一个类名。年代为约数。

items.en: The Latin verb acere meant 'to be sharp or sour', and it belongs with acer 'sharp' and acus 'needle', the same idea of a cutting edge.
items.cn: 拉丁动词 acere 意为「尖利、发酸」，与 acer「尖的」和 acus「针」同族，共享「有利刃」的念头。

items.en: Acidus was the adjective for a sour taste, used of fruit, wine and anything that made the mouth tighten.
items.cn: acidus 是表示酸味的形容词，用于水果、酒以及任何让口腔收紧的东西。

items.en: Old French carried the word into English in the medieval period, first as a description of taste and smell.
items.cn: 古法语在中世纪把该词带入英语，最初用来描述味道与气味。

items.en: As chemists sorted substances by their reactions, acid became the name of a class that turns litmus red and combines with alkalis.
items.cn: 当化学家按反应给物质分类时，acid 成了指一类能使石蕊变红、能与碱结合的物质的名字。

items.en: Later definitions widened the class to proton donors and then to electron-pair acceptors, while the old word stayed in place.
items.cn: 后来的定义把这一类先后扩展到质子给体与电子对受体，而旧词始终留在原位。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century the short noun was picked up as street slang for a particular drug; that use is informal and dated.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶，这个短名词被当作某种药物的街头俚语；这一用法不正式且已过时。

note.en: The first group shares the sour-taste stem; the second group holds words for chemical classes and qualities that are constantly mixed up with acid.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示酸味的词干；第二组是常与 acid 混淆的化学类别与性质词。

entries.definition: Having the properties of an acid, or tasting sour; it describes a quality, while acid can name the substance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 具有酸的性质或带酸味；它描述性质，而 acid 可以指物质本身。

entries.definition: The degree to which something is acid; it measures the property rather than naming a chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 某物呈酸性的程度；它衡量性质，而不命名化学物质。

entries.definition: To make something acid or more acid; it names the change, not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变酸或更酸；它命名变化，而非物质。

entries.definition: To make something slightly acid, especially in cooking; it is a smaller, gentler action than acidify.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物略带酸味，尤用于烹调；比 acidify 的动作更小更轻。

entries.definition: A substance that accepts protons or gives up electron pairs; acid and base are defined against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 接受质子或让出电子对的物质；酸与碱是相互对照定义的。

entries.definition: A base that dissolves in water, especially one of the old potash and soda substances; narrower than base.
entries.definitionCN: 能溶于水的碱，尤指旧时碳酸钾与苏打一类物质；比碱窄。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for the taste acid gives; it describes flavour and carries none of the chemical class meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 酸所带来味道的日常说法；它描述风味，不含化学类别的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin acidus 'sour' is the same sharpness that acer and acus carry.
normal.cn: 拉丁 acidus「酸的」与 acer、acus 共享同一种「尖利」。

normal.en: The family runs acid, acidic, acidity, acidify, acidification.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 acid、acidic、acidity、acidify、acidification。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: acid rain, acid test, stomach acid.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：酸雨、严峻考验、胃酸。

normal.en: The old gold test explains the phrase: a reagent sharp enough to show what a metal really is.
normal.cn: 旧时的验金法解释了那个说法：一种尖利到能显示金属真面目的试剂。

normal.en: Modern chemistry defines the class by protons given away or electron pairs accepted.
normal.cn: 现代化学用「让出质子」或「接受电子对」来定义这一类。

abstract.en: Picture a lemon wedge touched to the tongue and the whole face tightening at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一角柠檬碰到舌头，整张脸立刻收紧。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of strong liquid burning a clean line through a metal sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴强液体在金属片上烧出一道干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture a single sharp sentence that makes a room go quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一句尖利的话让整个房间安静下来。

examples.en: The lab stores strong acid in a locked cabinet.
examples.cn: 实验室把强酸锁在柜子里存放。

examples.en: Her acid tone made the apology sound hollow.
examples.cn: 她尖刻的语气让道歉听起来很空。

examples.en: The acid test came when the machine ran for a full week.
examples.cn: 真正的考验在机器连续运转一周时到来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a + cid（切）」——像刀一样切舌头的东西，就是酸

root: 拉丁 acidus「酸的」← acere「尖利、发酸」，与 acer「尖的」、acus「针」同族；经古法语入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one sharpness: the class of substances, the sour bottle in the kitchen, the taste, the cutting remark, polluted rain, the decisive test, the etching tool, the proton donor, and a street drug name.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一种尖利：一类物质、厨房里的酸味瓶、酸味本身、尖刻的话、被污染的雨、决定性检验、蚀刻工具、质子给体，以及一个街头药名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vat of pale liquid whose smell makes the tongue draw back before the nose registers it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一桶浅色液体，鼻子还没闻到，舌头就先缩了回去。

branches.en: THE SHARP QUALITY: the taste and the substance are felt as one thing before chemistry separates them.
branches.cn: 尖利的性质：在化学把它们分开之前，味道与物质被感受为同一件事。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN FORM: vinegar and lemon juice are the class met in bottles and fruit.
branches.cn: 厨房形态：醋与柠檬汁是这一类在瓶子和水果里的样子。

branches.en: THE DEFINED CLASS: the sour liquid is restated as any species that gives up a proton.
branches.cn: 被定义的那一类：酸味液体被重新表述为任何让出质子的物种。

branches.en: SHARPNESS APPLIED: rain becomes sour, a reagent proves gold, and a workshop cuts a pattern.
branches.cn: 被使用的尖利：雨变酸、试剂验金、作坊蚀刻图案。

branches.en: SHARPNESS TRANSFERRED: the same sting moves to a sentence and to a slang name.
branches.cn: 尖利被转移：同一种刺痛移到一句话和一个俚语名称上。

intro.en: Acid is a Latin adjective root with several productive English endings built on it.
intro.cn: acid 是一个拉丁形容词词根，英语在它上面长出了若干能产的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin acere and acidus stand behind acid, acidic, acidity and acidify, while acer and acus show the same sharp image in other words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 acere 与 acidus 支撑着 acid、acidic、acidity 与 acidify，而 acer 与 acus 在别的词里展现同一个尖利图景。

items.structure: Latin verb, 'to be sharp or sour'
items.example: The root supplies the sense of a cutting taste.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「割舌的味道」这一感觉。
