items.example: The adjective came into English as a taste word.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词作为味道词进入英语。

items.structure: adjective ending meaning 'of the nature of'
items.example: The ending turns the noun into a quality word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成性质词。

items.example: The ending turns the quality into a measurable state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把性质变成可测量的状态。

items.example: The ending produces the verb of making something sour.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「使变酸」的动词。

items.example: The noun names the class and the adjective the quality.
items.exampleCN: 名词指这一类，形容词指这种性质。

items.example: The soil here is slightly acidic.
items.exampleCN: 这里的土壤略带酸性。

items.example: Winemakers watch the acidity closely.
items.exampleCN: 酿酒者密切关注酸度。

items.example: The rain acidified the lake over decades.
items.exampleCN: 降雨在数十年间使湖水酸化。

items.structure: acidify plus the action noun ending
items.example: Ocean acidification worries marine biologists.
items.exampleCN: 海洋酸化令海洋生物学家担忧。

derivatives.zh: 由 acid 加性质词尾构成，义为「酸性的」
由 acid 加状态词尾构成，义为「酸性；酸度」
由 acid 加使动词尾构成，义为「使变酸」
由 acidify 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「酸化过程」

definition_zh: 酸性；酸度；酸味；（液体的）含酸量
definition_en: the quality or degree of being acid, or the amount of acid present in a liquid
core_image: 化验台上排着几只样瓶，滴定管一滴一滴落下，颜色一变就记下一个数字
scene: 化验员把碱液一滴一滴加进样瓶，颜色刚转，他就记下这批醋的酸度。A titration gives the acidity of the batch before it is bottled.
sceneCN: 这里 acidity 指样品呈酸性的程度或含酸量（第 2 个义项：可测量的酸度）；句意：滴定在装瓶前给出这一批的酸度。图中可辨识物件：样瓶、滴定管、变色液面、记录本。

derivatives.zh: 由 acid 加性质词尾构成，义为「酸性的」
由 acid 加使动词尾构成，义为「使变酸」
由 acidify 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「酸化过程」

senses.title: The state of being sour
senses.definition: the quality of tasting sharp and sour
senses.definitionCN: 尝起来尖利发酸的性质
senses.example: The green apples were prized for their acidity.
senses.exampleCN: 这些青苹果因酸味而受青睐。
senses.why: The noun is the quality form of acid, so the oldest sense is simply the sour character that acid things share.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 acid 的性质形式，因此最早的义项就是酸物共有的那种酸味特征。

senses.title: A measurable acid content
senses.definition: the amount of acid in a solution, usually found by titration or by a meter reading
senses.definitionCN: 溶液中所含酸的量，通常由滴定或仪器读数得出
senses.example: A titration gives the acidity of the batch before it is bottled.
senses.exampleCN: 滴定在装瓶前给出这一批的酸度。
senses.why: Once chemists could measure the quality, the abstract noun became a number attached to a particular liquid.
senses.whyCN: 化学家能测量这种性质之后，这个抽象名词就变成了附在某种液体上的数字。

senses.title: Acid strength in chemical terms
senses.definition: the extent to which a substance behaves as an acid, expressed as its tendency to give up protons
senses.definitionCN: 某物质表现酸性程度的大小，以其让出质子的倾向表示
senses.example: The acidity of the two acids differs by several orders of magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种酸的酸强度相差好几个数量级。
senses.why: Chemical language separates strength from concentration, and this noun carries the strength side.
senses.whyCN: 化学用语把强度与浓度分开，而这个词承载的是强度那一面。

senses.title: Stomach acid level
senses.definition: the concentration of acid in the stomach, which affects digestion and comfort
senses.definitionCN: 胃中酸的浓度，影响消化与舒适感
senses.example: Too much acidity in the stomach can cause burning.
senses.exampleCN: 胃里酸度过高会引起烧灼感。
senses.why: Medicine applies the measurable sense to a body part, where the number has direct consequences for how a person feels.
senses.whyCN: 医学把可测量的义项用在身体部位上，那里的数字直接影响人的感受。

senses.title: Soil that will not suit crops
senses.titleCN: 不适合作物的土壤酸度
senses.definition: the acid condition of soil, which determines which plants can grow and what must be added
senses.definitionCN: 土壤的酸性状况，决定哪些植物能生长、需要加入什么
senses.example: High acidity in the field forced the farmers to add lime.
senses.exampleCN: 田里的高酸度迫使农民施石灰。
senses.why: Agriculture uses the word as a property of land, something to be corrected rather than merely noted.
senses.whyCN: 农业把这个词当作土地的一种性质，一种需要纠正而不仅是记录的东西。

senses.title: Sourness in rain, lakes and sea
senses.titleCN: 雨水、湖泊与海水中的酸度
senses.definition: the acid level of natural water, raised by absorbed gases or dissolved minerals
senses.definitionCN: 天然水体中的酸水平，因吸收气体或溶解矿物而升高
senses.example: Ocean acidity has risen since the industrial era.
senses.exampleCN: 自工业时代以来海洋酸度上升了。
senses.why: Environmental science scales the measurement up to whole bodies of water, where it becomes a slow, cumulative change.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把测量放大到整个水体，在那里它成了一种缓慢累积的变化。

senses.title: A sharp quality in a voice
senses.definition: a biting or bitter tone in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 言语或文字中尖利刻薄的语气
senses.example: The acidity of her reply surprised the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句回复的尖刻让在场的人都意外。
senses.why: The taste sense extends to sound, because a sharp remark and a sour fruit produce the same wince.
senses.whyCN: 味觉义延伸到声音，因为尖刻的话与酸果引起同样的缩舌反应。

senses.title: The lively tartness in wine or coffee
senses.titleCN: 葡萄酒或咖啡中活泼的酸感
senses.definition: the fresh, structured sourness that gives a drink balance and keeps it from tasting flat
senses.definitionCN: 赋予饮品平衡、使其不显呆板的那种清新有骨架的酸感
senses.example: Tasters praised the coffee for its bright acidity.
senses.exampleCN: 品鉴者称赞这款咖啡明亮的酸感。
senses.why: In tasting notes the same measurement becomes a virtue, because a little acid is what keeps a drink alive.
senses.whyCN: 在品鉴记录里，同一项测量变成一种优点，因为少量酸正是让饮品有生气的东西。

intro.en: Acidity is the noun of quality built on Latin acidus 'sour'; it reached English through French in the early modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: acidity 是在拉丁 acidus「酸的」之上构成的性质名词，近代早期经法语进入英语；年代为约数。

items.en: Acidus 'sour' came from acere 'to be sharp or sour', the same stock as acer 'sharp' and acus 'needle'.
items.cn: acidus「酸的」出自 acere「尖利、发酸」，与 acer「尖的」、acus「针」同源。

items.en: Latin formed a quality noun in -itas, naming the state of being sour; this is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.cn: 拉丁语用表示性质的名词词尾构成名词，命名「呈酸的状态」；这就是英语词的直接祖形。

items.en: French carried the noun forward, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries alongside the adjective acid.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词继续带下来，英语在 16、17 世纪与形容词 acid 一同借入。

items.en: As acid became a class name, the quality noun was pulled into the laboratory and given numbers by titration.
items.cn: 当 acid 成为类名，这个性质名词也被拉进实验室，并由滴定赋予数字。

items.en: Medicine, agriculture, oceanography and tasting notes each adopted the measured sense for their own liquids and lands.
items.cn: 医学、农业、海洋学与品鉴记录各自为自家的液体与土地采用了这一可测量的义项。

items.en: First date uncertain: the noun is recorded from the early modern period, but the precise earliest English citation is not securely fixed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个名词在近代早期已有记录，但确切的英语最早引文并未被牢固确定。

note.en: The first group shares the sour stem and differs in word class; the second group holds neighbouring measures and qualities of solutions.
note.cn: 第一组共享酸味词干而词类不同；第二组是溶液中相邻的度量与性质。

entries.definition: The chemical itself, or the sharp taste; acidity is the measured quality that substance has.
entries.definitionCN: 化学物质本身，或那种尖利的味道；acidity 则是该物质所具有的可测性质。

entries.definition: Describing something that has acid properties; it says what kind of thing it is, not how much of the property it has.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物具有酸的性质；它说明属于哪一类，而不说这种性质有多少。

entries.definition: To make something acid; it names a change, while acidity names the resulting measurable state.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变酸；它命名变化，而 acidity 命名变化后形成的可测状态。

entries.definition: A fixed phrase for the measured value; here the noun is a modifier inside a longer term.
entries.definitionCN: 指测得数值的固定说法；这里该名词是更长术语里的修饰成分。

entries.definition: A number on a logarithmic scale for acid and base strength; acidity is the property, pH is one way of reporting it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示酸碱强弱的对数尺度上的数字；acidity 是性质，pH 是报告它的一种方式。

entries.definition: The everyday quality of being sour; it stays in the mouth and never becomes a laboratory measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 日常所说的「酸」这一性质；它停留在味觉层面，从不变成实验室测量。

entries.definition: The measured capacity of water to neutralise acid; it is the mirror number on the other side of neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 水抵偿酸的能力的度量；它是中性另一侧与之相对的数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: acid plus the quality ending -ity: the state of being acid.
normal.cn: acid 加表示性质的名词词尾：呈酸的状态。

normal.en: The family runs acid, acidic, acidity, acidify, acidification.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 acid、acidic、acidity、acidify、acidification。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the measured side: high acidity, soil acidity, acidity level.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出可测量的一面：高酸度、土壤酸度、酸度水平。

normal.en: A titration is the standard picture: one drop changes the colour and the number is read.
normal.cn: 滴定是标准画面：一滴落下、颜色一变，数字就被读出。

normal.en: Tasters treat a little acidity as a virtue, not a fault.
normal.cn: 品鉴者把少量酸度当作优点，而不是缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a row of sample bottles whose colours shift one shade at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一排样瓶，颜色一格一格地变化。

abstract.en: Picture a lemonade that is pleasant until one more squeeze makes the mouth ache.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯柠檬水本来宜人，再挤一下就让嘴发酸。

abstract.en: Picture a lake slowly turning sour over decades, with nobody able to point to a single day.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湖在数十年里慢慢变酸，却没人能指出是哪一天开始的。

examples.en: Winemakers test the acidity before deciding when to harvest.
examples.cn: 酿酒者在决定采收时间前先测酸度。

examples.en: The acidity of the soil limits which crops will grow.
examples.cn: 土壤的酸度限制了能种哪些作物。

examples.en: Doctors asked whether stomach acidity had changed.
examples.cn: 医生询问胃酸度是否发生了变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「acid（酸）+ ity（性质）」——酸的程度，就是酸度

root: 拉丁 acidus「酸的」+ 表示性质的名词词尾；经法语入英语，指呈酸的状态或可测的含酸量。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measured sourness: the plain state, the number from a titration, the chemical strength, the stomach, the field, natural waters, a biting voice, and the prized tartness of a good drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种被量度的酸：朴素的状态、滴定得出的数字、化学强度、胃、田地、天然水体、尖刻的语调，以及好饮品里被称许的酸感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a burette dripping into a sample bottle until the colour turns and a figure is written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：滴定管滴入样瓶，颜色一转，就记下一个数字。

branches.en: THE QUALITY ITSELF: before any instrument, acidity is what makes the mouth tighten.
branches.cn: 性质本身：在任何仪器之前，酸度就是让口腔收紧的那种东西。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SIDE: the quality becomes a number, and chemistry separates strength from mere concentration.
branches.cn: 可测量的一面：性质变成数字，化学又把强度与单纯的浓度分开。

branches.en: BODY AND LAND: the same number is felt in a stomach and corrected in a field.
branches.cn: 身体与土地：同一个数字在胃里被感受到，在田里被纠正。

branches.en: THE LARGE SCALE: lakes and seas accumulate the change where no single day can be blamed.
branches.cn: 更大的尺度：湖泊与海洋累积这种变化，找不出该归咎的某一天。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED VALUE: sharpness in a voice is a fault, while tartness in a drink is a praised balance.
branches.cn: 转移的价值：语调里的尖利是缺点，而饮品里的酸感却是受称赞的平衡。

intro.en: Acidity is a base word plus a quality ending, and the same base supports a whole family of English words.
intro.cn: acidity 是一个基础词加一个性质词尾，而同一个基础词支撑起整个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin acidus and its noun of quality sit behind this word, while acer and acus show the same sharp image elsewhere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 acidus 及其性质名词是这个词的祖形，而 acer 与 acus 在别处展现同一个尖利图景。

items.example: The base word names both the thing and the taste.
items.exampleCN: 基础词同时命名事物与味道。

items.structure: Latin noun ending for state or quality
items.example: The ending turns an adjective into a measurable state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成可测的状态。

items.meaning: the state or degree of being acid
items.example: The acidity of the batch was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这一批的酸度被记录了下来。

items.example: The groundwater is mildly acidic.
items.exampleCN: 地下水略带酸性。

items.example: Pollution acidified the stream.
items.exampleCN: 污染使小溪酸化。

items.structure: acidify plus the action noun ending
items.example: Acidification changed the lake's fish population.
items.exampleCN: 酸化改变了湖里的鱼类组成。

items.structure: acid plus a diminutive verb ending plus a state ending
items.example: The recipe calls for acidulated water.
items.exampleCN: 这个做法需要略带酸味的水。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring acid strength
items.example: The acidimeter gave a reading within a minute.
items.exampleCN: 酸度计一分钟内给出了读数。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「酸；酸的」
由基础词加性质词尾构成，义为「酸性的」
由基础词加使动词尾构成，义为「使变酸」

definition_zh: 底部；基座；基础；基地；垒；（化学）碱；词基；（数学）底数
definition_en: the lowest part or supporting foundation of something, the main place from which an activity operates, or a substance that reacts with an acid
core_image: 石匠先在坑里铺一层平整大石，再往上砌砖，整座塔的重量都由这一层接住
scene: 修塔的工匠先在坑底铺一层平整的大石，然后才往上砌第一层砖。The masons set the base of the tower before the first course of stone.
sceneCN: 这里 base 指承接整座建筑重量的最下层部分（第 1 个义项：底部、基座）；句意：石匠先安放塔的基座，再砌第一层石头。图中可辨识物件：基坑、大石块、砖层、吊绳。

pos.zh: 底部；基座；基础；基地；垒；碱；词基；底数

derivatives.zh: 由 base 加表示「属于……的」形容词词尾构成，义为「基本的」
由 base 加表示场所的名词词尾构成，义为「地下室」
由 base 加表示「没有」的形容词成分构成，义为「无根据的」
由 base 与表示「线」的成分复合而成，义为「基准线」

senses.title: The lowest supporting part
senses.definition: the bottom part of a structure, on which the rest rests
senses.definitionCN: 结构的最下部分，其余部分都压在它上面
senses.example: The masons set the base of the tower before the first course of stone.
senses.exampleCN: 石匠先安放塔的基座，再砌第一层石头。
senses.why: The Greek source meant a step or pedestal, so the physical support is the sense from which the rest grew.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源指台阶或柱础，因此物理上的承重部分是其余各义生长出来的那个义项。

senses.title: The foundation of an argument
senses.definition: the facts, evidence or principles on which a claim, system or relationship rests
senses.definitionCN: 主张、体系或关系所依靠的事实、证据或原则
senses.example: The charges rest on a base of solid evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这些指控建立在扎实证据的基础之上。
senses.why: Reasoning is pictured as a building: what holds it up is called by the name of the stone course at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 推理被想成一座建筑：托住它的东西，就用最底下那层石头的名称来称呼。

senses.title: The place an activity works from
senses.definition: the main centre from which an organization, military force or expedition operates
senses.definitionCN: 某个组织、军队或考察队展开行动的主要中心
senses.example: The rescue team returned to its base before nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队在入夜前回到基地。
senses.why: A base is where supplies and people are kept, so it functions as the ground on which operations stand.
senses.whyCN: 基地是存放补给与人员的地方，因此它起着「让行动得以立足的地面」的作用。

senses.title: One of the four corners in baseball
senses.titleCN: 棒球场上的四个垒位之一
senses.definition: one of the four stations a runner must touch to score
senses.definitionCN: 跑垒者必须依次触到才能得分的四个站点之一
senses.example: The runner slid into third base just ahead of the throw.
senses.exampleCN: 跑垒者在传球到达前滑上三垒。
senses.why: The station is a fixed mark on the ground, so the everyday word for a supporting point was borrowed for it.
senses.whyCN: 垒是地面上一个固定标记，于是表示「支撑点」的日常词被借来指它。

senses.title: The substance that neutralises acid
senses.definition: a substance that accepts protons or gives up electron pairs, reacting with an acid to form a salt
senses.definitionCN: 接受质子或让出电子对、与酸反应生成盐的物质
senses.example: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base.
senses.exampleCN: 氢氧化钠是一种强碱。
senses.why: Chemists borrowed the word for the substance on which an acid spends its strength, picturing it as the ground that receives the attack.
senses.whyCN: 化学家借这个词指「承接酸的力量」的物质，把它想象成接受攻击的地面。

senses.title: The part a word is built on
senses.definition: the form of a word to which endings and prefixes are added
senses.definitionCN: 词加上词尾与词缀时所依附的那个形式
senses.example: The teacher wrote the base on the board and added endings to it.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在黑板上写出词基，再往上加词尾。
senses.why: Grammar uses the building image again: affixes are attached to a supporting form underneath them.
senses.whyCN: 语法再次使用建筑的图景：词缀被加到下面那个起支撑作用的形式上。

senses.title: The number raised to a power
senses.definition: the number that is multiplied by itself in a power or used as the foundation of a number system
senses.definitionCN: 乘方中自我相乘的那个数，或数制所依据的那个数
senses.example: In base ten, each place is ten times the one to its right.
senses.exampleCN: 在十进制中，每一位是右边一位的十倍。
senses.why: Mathematics treats the base as the fixed ground from which the whole expression is built upward.
senses.whyCN: 数学把底数当作固定的地面，整个表达式都从它往上搭起。

senses.title: The first coat under a finish
senses.titleCN: 面层下面的第一道涂层
senses.definition: the layer painted or applied first, on which later coats are laid
senses.definitionCN: 最先涂上、供后续涂层附着的那一层
senses.example: A grey base hides the patchy colour of the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 一层灰色底漆遮住了旧墙斑驳的颜色。
senses.why: Painting repeats the physical picture: the lowest layer is what everything above depends on.
senses.whyCN: 涂装重复了那个物理图景：最下面的一层，是上面一切所依赖的东西。

intro.en: Base comes through Old French and Latin from Greek basis, 'a step or pedestal'. A separate adjective base meaning 'low, mean' has a different origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: base 经古法语与拉丁语来自希腊 basis「台阶、柱础」；另有一个意为「卑劣、低级」的同形形容词，来源不同。年代为约数。

items.en: The Greek verb bainein meant 'to go or step', and from it came basis, a thing one steps on.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 bainein 意为「走、踏」，由它产生 basis，即脚所踏之物。

items.en: Basis meant a step, a pedestal or a foundation, used of feet, columns and the ground of an argument alike.
items.cn: basis 指台阶、柱础或基础，脚、柱子与论证的地面都用它。

items.en: Latin borrowed basis unchanged in form and kept both the physical and the argumentative senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语原形借入 basis，并同时保留物理义与论证义。

items.en: Old French base entered English in the medieval period, first of the lower part of a building or a column.
items.cn: 古法语 base 在中世纪进入英语，最初指建筑或柱子的下部。

items.en: Eighteenth-century chemistry named the substance that receives an acid a base, and later centuries added the military, sporting, grammatical and numerical uses.
items.cn: 18 世纪化学把承接酸的那种物质命名为碱，后来的世纪又加入军事、体育、语法与数制用法。

items.en: The adjective base meaning 'low or mean' comes through Old French bas from Late Latin bassus 'short, low'; it is not a relative of the Greek word and should not be read as part of this family.
items.cn: 意为「卑劣、低级」的同形形容词，经古法语 bas 上溯到晚期拉丁 bassus「矮、低」；它与这个希腊语词并非同族，不应算入本词族。

note.en: The first group shares the same root and is often confused; the second group holds the neighbouring supports and the chemical opposite word.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根，常被混淆；第二组是相邻的「支撑」说法与化学上的相对词。

entries.definition: A borrowed Latin noun for the underlying principle or the main part; it is close in meaning but keeps a more formal, abstract tone.
entries.definitionCN: 直接借入的拉丁名词，指根本原则或主要部分；意义接近，但语气更正式、更抽象。

entries.definition: Describing what is fundamental or simple; it names a quality rather than a supporting part.
entries.definitionCN: 描述根本或简单之物；它命名性质，而不是承重部分。

entries.definition: The storey under a building; the word adds a place ending to base and names a space, not the support itself.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑下面的一层；这个词在 base 后加表示场所的词尾，命名空间而非承重本身。

entries.definition: A low-pitched sound or instrument, from a different Latin word for 'low'; the spelling looks close but the origin is separate.
entries.definitionCN: 低音或低音乐器，来自另一个表示「低」的拉丁词；拼写相近，来源却不同。

entries.definition: The solid layer put under a building, or the principle under an institution; it stresses deliberate laying rather than mere support.
entries.definitionCN: 铺在建筑下面的坚固层，或机构所依据的原则；它强调有意铺设，而非单纯承重。

entries.definition: The secure grip or level ground a structure or person stands on; more concrete than the abstract uses of base.
entries.definitionCN: 结构或人所站的稳固立足处；比 base 的抽象用法更具体。

entries.definition: The substance that gives up protons to a base; the two are defined only against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 把质子让给碱的物质；两者只能相互对照定义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek basis 'step or pedestal' is the picture: everything else stands on it.
normal.cn: 希腊 basis「台阶、柱础」就是那幅画：别的一切都站在它上面。

normal.en: The family runs base, basis, basic, basement, baseless, baseline.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 base、basis、basic、basement、baseless、baseline。

normal.en: Fixed phrases spread across fields: military base, base of the tower, base ten, base layer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分布在多个领域：军事基地、塔基、十进制、底层。

normal.en: Chemistry pictures the base as the ground that receives what an acid throws at it.
normal.cn: 化学把碱想象成承受酸所投之物的一片地面。

normal.en: The adjective meaning 'low' looks the same but comes from another Latin word.
normal.cn: 意为「低劣」的同形形容词看起来一样，却来自另一个拉丁词。

abstract.en: Picture a tower standing only because one flat stone holds all the weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔能立住，只因为一块平石接住了全部重量。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that collapses the moment one supporting fact is removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个论证，一旦抽掉一条支撑事实就整个垮掉。

abstract.en: Picture a stage whose floor is never seen but holds every performer.
abstract.cn: 想象一座舞台，地板从不被看见，却托住每一个表演者。

examples.en: The company moved its base to a smaller city.
examples.cn: 公司把基地迁到了较小的城市。

examples.en: Every conclusion here is based on the same three measurements.
examples.cn: 这里每个结论都建立在同样三项测量之上。

examples.en: Lime is added when the soil is too much of a base.
examples.cn: 土壤碱性过强时就要加石灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ba（吧）+ se（座）」——最下面的那座，就是基座

root: 希腊 basis「台阶、柱础」← bainein「走、踏」，经拉丁 basis 与古法语 base 入英语；同形形容词「卑劣的」出自晚期拉丁 bassus，非本词族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one supporting layer: the stone under a tower, the evidence under a claim, the place an operation starts from, a station on a field, the substance under an acid's attack, the form under affixes, the number under a power, and the coat under a finish.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个承重层：塔下的石、主张下的证据、行动出发的地点、场上的垒位、承受酸攻击的物质、词缀依附的形式、乘方所依的数、面层下的第一道涂层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one flat stone at the bottom of a pit, carrying a whole tower above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：坑底一块平石，托住上面整座塔。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL LAYER: the lowest stone is the original sense and the model for everything else.
branches.cn: 物理层：最下面的石头是最早的义项，也是其余各义的模型。

branches.en: WHAT RESTS ON IT: evidence holds a claim up, and a word form holds its endings up.
branches.cn: 依托其上的东西：证据托住主张，词干托住词尾。

branches.en: WHERE THINGS STAND: an operation has a home base, and a runner has a station to reach.
branches.cn: 立足之处：行动有大本营，跑垒者有要抵达的垒位。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL RECEIVER: the base is the ground on which an acid spends itself.
branches.cn: 化学上的承接者：碱就是酸把力气用掉的那片地面。

branches.en: THE FIXED FLOOR: a numeral system and a first coat both build upward from a set layer.
branches.cn: 固定的底板：数制与第一道涂层都从一个既定层往上搭。

intro.en: Base is a Greek-derived noun that has collected a large English family through common endings.
intro.cn: base 是一个希腊语来源的名词，通过常见词尾聚集出一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek basis passed into Latin unchanged and gave English base, basis and basic; the separate Latin bassus is not part of this group.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 basis 原样进入拉丁语，衍生出英语 base、basis 与 basic；另一个拉丁词 bassus 不属于这一组。

items.meaning: a thing stepped on; a foundation
items.example: The root supplies the picture of a stone under a foot.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「脚下一块石」的画面。

items.meaning: the lower part; a centre; a chemical receiver
items.meaningCN: 下部；中心；化学上的承接物
items.example: One word covers stone, argument and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词覆盖石头、论证与化学。

items.structure: adjective ending meaning 'of the nature of'
items.example: The ending produces the adjective for fundamental things.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示「根本」的形容词。

items.example: The ending names the storey below the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾命名地面下的那层空间。

items.example: The boxes were stored in the basement.
items.exampleCN: 箱子存放在地下室里。

items.example: The basic rule is easy to state.
items.exampleCN: 基本规则很容易说明。

items.example: The rumour was baseless.
items.exampleCN: 那个传言毫无根据。

items.structure: base plus the word for a line
items.example: The measurements were taken from a baseline.
items.exampleCN: 测量从一个基准线开始。

items.example: The film is based on a true story.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片根据真实故事改编。

latinEntries.structure: basis, basis (n., third declension, from Greek)

derivatives.zh: 由 base 加性质词尾构成，义为「基本的」
由 base 加场所词尾构成，义为「地下室」
由 base 加表示「没有」的成分构成，义为「无根据的」
由 base 与表示「线」的成分复合而成，义为「基准线」

definition_zh: 碱性的；含碱的；（土壤、水体）偏碱的
definition_en: having the properties of an alkali, especially having a pH above seven
core_image: 菜园里的土被撒了一层白灰，蓝莓的叶子随后一片片发黄
scene: 菜园角落撒过石灰，土变得偏碱，旁边的蓝莓叶一片片发黄。The soil is too alkaline for blueberries, so the bushes yellow.
sceneCN: 这里 alkaline 指含碱、酸碱度偏高的性质（第 1 个义项：呈碱性的）；句意：土壤碱性过强，不适于蓝莓，于是灌木发黄。图中可辨识物件：石灰、菜畦、发黄的叶片、浇水壶。

derivatives.zh: 由 alkaline 加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「碱性；碱度」
由 alkaline 加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」
由 alkali 加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」
由 alkali 加医学病态词尾构成，义为「碱中毒」

senses.title: Having a pH above seven
senses.definition: having a pH greater than seven, so that it neutralises acid
senses.definitionCN: 酸碱度高于七，因而能抵偿酸
senses.example: The soil is too alkaline for blueberries, so the bushes yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤碱性过强，不适于蓝莓，于是灌木发黄。
senses.why: The adjective simply says a substance has the character of an alkali, the class of bases that dissolve in water.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是说某物具有碱的性格，而碱是能溶于水的那一类碱。

senses.title: A solution that turns litmus blue
senses.definition: describing a solution that turns red litmus blue and feels slippery rather than sour
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种使红色石蕊变蓝、摸起来滑腻而不酸的溶液
senses.example: Soapy water is mildly alkaline on the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 肥皂水对皮肤有轻微的碱性。
senses.why: The laboratory test gives the quality a visible sign, so the adjective is used of any liquid that shows that sign.
senses.whyCN: 实验室检验给这种性质一个可见标志，因此凡是显出该标志的液体都用这个形容词。

senses.title: Ground that will not suit acid-loving plants
senses.titleCN: 不适宜喜酸植物的土地
senses.definition: describing soil whose high pH blocks the uptake of some nutrients and suits a different range of crops
senses.definitionCN: 描述酸碱度偏高、阻碍某些养分吸收而适合另一类作物的土壤
senses.example: Farmers added gypsum to the alkaline field.
senses.exampleCN: 农民向碱性田块施用石膏。
senses.why: Agriculture turns the chemical property into a practical verdict about land and what will grow there.
senses.whyCN: 农业把化学性质变成对土地与作物的实用判断。

senses.title: The kind of battery in a torch
senses.definition: describing a dry cell that uses an alkaline electrolyte rather than an acidic one
senses.definitionCN: 描述使用碱性电解液而非酸性电解液的干电池
senses.example: An alkaline battery lasts longer in the winter torch.
senses.exampleCN: 碱性电池在冬季手电里更耐用。
senses.why: The adjective labels one working design by the chemistry inside it, so the term moved from the lab to the shop shelf.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词按内部的化学来给一种设计贴标签，于是这个术语从实验室走到了货架。

senses.title: A group of reactive metals
senses.definition: describing the group of metals, including calcium and magnesium, whose oxides were once called earths
senses.definitionCN: 描述包括钙与镁在内的一组金属，其氧化物旧称「土」
senses.example: Calcium belongs to the alkaline earth metals.
senses.exampleCN: 钙属于碱土金属。
senses.why: Old chemistry called the oxides of these metals earths, and because those earths behaved as bases the group took the name.
senses.whyCN: 旧化学把这些金属的氧化物称作「土」，而这些土表现碱的性质，这一族因此得名。

senses.title: A diet said to balance body chemistry
senses.titleCN: 号称能平衡体内酸碱的饮食
senses.definition: describing food or a diet promoted as raising the body's pH, a claim that mainstream nutrition does not accept
senses.definitionCN: 描述被宣传为能提高体内酸碱度的食物或饮食，这一说法并未被主流营养学接受
senses.example: The booklet sells an alkaline diet to worried readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子向担心的读者推销碱性饮食。
senses.why: Popular writing borrows the chemical label for a health promise, so the adjective now appears in advertising as well as in journals.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作借用这个化学标签来作健康承诺，于是这个形容词既出现在期刊里，也出现在广告里。

senses.title: A reaction run under basic conditions
senses.titleCN: 在碱性条件下进行的反应
senses.definition: describing a process carried out in a solution with a pH above seven, such as alkaline hydrolysis
senses.definitionCN: 描述在酸碱度高于七的溶液中进行的操作，如碱性水解
senses.example: The alkaline hydrolysis broke the ester apart quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 碱性水解很快把酯拆开。
senses.why: In procedure writing the adjective marks the conditions of a step, standing in for the whole chemical environment.
senses.whyCN: 在流程写作里，这个形容词标出某一步的条件，代指整个化学环境。

senses.title: A lake or spring with unusual chemistry
senses.titleCN: 化学性质特殊的湖泊或泉水
senses.definition: describing a natural water body whose dissolved minerals keep it strongly basic
senses.definitionCN: 描述溶解矿物使其保持强碱性的天然水体
senses.example: Few fish survive in the alkaline lake.
senses.exampleCN: 能在碱性湖里存活的鱼很少。
senses.why: Field science applies the adjective to whole landscapes, where the chemistry is a lasting feature rather than a test result.
senses.whyCN: 野外科学把这个形容词用在整片景观上，那里的化学是持久特征，而非一次检验结果。

intro.en: Alkaline is built on alkali, an Arabic-derived word for the ashes of a salt-tolerant plant, plus an adjective ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: alkaline 由 alkali 加形容词词尾构成，而 alkali 是一个源自阿拉伯语、指耐盐植物灰烬的词。年代为约数。

items.en: Arabic al-qily named the calcined ashes of saltwort, a plant burned to make a cleansing substance; al- is the article and qily the ashes.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qily 指盐生植物的煅烧灰，那种植物被烧成清洗用的物质；al- 是冠词，qily 是灰。

items.en: Medieval Latin took the Arabic term as alkali and used it for the soda and potash substances of early chemistry.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这个阿拉伯术语借作 alkali，用来指早期化学中的苏打与碳酸钾类物质。

items.en: English adopted alkali in the seventeenth century, when experiments with salts and ashes were expanding.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪采用 alkali，当时关于盐与灰的实验正在扩展。

items.en: The adjective added a suffix meaning 'of the nature of', first in scientific writing, to describe substances that behaved like these ashes.
items.cn: 形容词形式加上了表示「具有……性质」的词尾，最初见于科学写作，用来描述表现得像这些灰的物质。

items.en: Later the word spread from chemistry to soil, water, batteries, diets and rock types, keeping the core idea of a basic reaction.
items.cn: 后来这个词从化学扩展到土壤、水体、电池、饮食与岩石类型，始终保留「呈碱性反应」的核心意思。

items.en: Source uncertain for details: the exact plant behind the Arabic term and the precise first English use of the adjective are not securely established.
items.cn: 细节来源不确定：阿拉伯语词所指的确切植物，以及该形容词在英语中的确切首次使用，都未被牢固确立。

note.en: The first group shares the alkali stem and differs by word class; the second group holds the neighbouring chemical labels.
note.cn: 第一组共享 alkali 词干而词类不同；第二组是相邻的化学标签。

entries.definition: A soluble base, especially the old soda and potash substances; alkaline describes something that has this character.
entries.definitionCN: 可溶性碱，尤指旧时的苏打与碳酸钾类物质；alkaline 描述具有这种性格的东西。

entries.definition: The degree to which water or a solution is alkaline; it is the number, while alkaline is the label.
entries.definitionCN: 水或溶液呈碱性的程度；它是数字，而 alkaline 是标签。

entries.definition: To make something alkaline; it names the change, not the state.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变碱；它命名变化，而非状态。

entries.definition: A fixed product name in which the adjective picks out one electrolyte design.
entries.definitionCN: 固定的产品名称，其中这个形容词点出一种电解液设计。

entries.definition: In chemistry, describing a substance that accepts protons; it is the technical partner of alkaline, which is more common in everyday and environmental writing.
entries.definitionCN: 化学上描述接受质子的物质；它是 alkaline 的技术同义说法，而后者更常见于日常与环境写作。

entries.definition: Describing a substance with a pH below seven; it is the direct opposite of alkaline on the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 描述酸碱度低于七的物质；它是同一尺度上与 alkaline 正好相反的说法。

entries.definition: Describing water that contains dissolved salt; saltiness is a different property from alkalinity and the two often travel together in lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 描述含溶解盐的水；咸是与碱性不同的性质，二者在湖泊中常同时出现。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: alkali plus the adjective ending: having the character of those plant ashes.
normal.cn: alkali 加形容词词尾：具有那种植物灰的性格。

normal.en: The family runs alkali, alkaline, alkalinity, alkalize, alkalosis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 alkali、alkaline、alkalinity、alkalize、alkalosis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases span lab and shop: alkaline solution, alkaline soil, alkaline battery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配横跨实验室与商店：碱性溶液、碱性土壤、碱性电池。

normal.en: The word began with ashes of a salt-tolerant plant burned for cleansing.
normal.cn: 这个词起于一种耐盐植物的灰，那种灰被烧出来用于清洗。

normal.en: On the pH scale, alkaline simply means above the middle.
normal.cn: 在酸碱度尺度上，碱性不过是「高于中间」。

abstract.en: Picture a white powder spread on a garden bed and the leaves turning pale soon after.
abstract.cn: 想象一层白粉撒在菜畦上，随后叶子一片片变淡。

abstract.en: Picture a bar of soap that slides out of a dry hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肥皂从干手里滑出去。

abstract.en: Picture a lake so unusual that only a few species can live in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湖水特殊到只有少数物种能生存。

examples.en: The river below the quarry stays alkaline all year.
examples.cn: 采石场下游的河水全年呈碱性。

examples.en: Alkaline soils need different fertilisers from acid ones.
examples.cn: 碱性土壤需要与酸性土壤不同的肥料。

examples.en: She swapped the torch to an alkaline battery before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨前她把火把换成了碱性电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「alkali（碱）+ ne」——带着碱的性格，就是碱性的

root: 阿拉伯 al-qily「盐生植物的灰」→ 中世纪拉丁 alkali → 英语 alkali + 形容词词尾；指呈碱性、酸碱度偏高。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one basic character: the pH label, the litmus test, the soil verdict, the battery design, the metal group, the diet claim, the reaction conditions, and a whole lake.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种碱的性格：酸碱度标签、石蕊检验、土壤判断、电池设计、金属族名、饮食宣传、反应条件，以及一整片湖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white lime spread on a bed, and leaves paling because the ground has turned basic.
core.cn: 核心意象：石灰撒在菜畦上，因为土变碱，叶子随之发白。

branches.en: THE LABEL AND ITS SIGN: the number above seven, and the colour change that makes it visible.
branches.cn: 标签与标志：高于七的数字，以及使它可见的变色。

branches.en: THE LAND VERDICT: the same property decides which crops a field can carry.
branches.cn: 土地判断：同一性质决定一块田能种什么。

branches.en: NAMES IN THE WORLD: the adjective labels a battery design and a group of metals.
branches.cn: 世间的名称：这个形容词给一种电池设计与一组金属贴标签。

branches.en: CLAIMS AND CONDITIONS: advertising borrows the word, and procedure writing uses it to set a reaction.
branches.cn: 宣传与条件：广告借用这个词，流程写作则用它设定反应条件。

branches.en: THE LANDSCAPE: a lake can be alkaline for its whole life, not just in one test.
branches.cn: 景观：一片湖可以一生呈碱性，而不只在一次检验里。

intro.en: Alkaline is an Arabic-derived noun plus an adjective ending, and the family extends into chemistry, medicine and industry.
intro.cn: alkaline 是一个阿拉伯语来源的名词加形容词词尾，这个词族延伸到化学、医学与工业。

latinIntro.en: The word reached Europe through medieval Latin, but its root is Arabic; Latin supplies only the adjective and noun endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经中世纪拉丁语进入欧洲，但词根来自阿拉伯语；拉丁语只提供形容词与名词词尾，因此不列词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The root names the ashes that were burned for cleansing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被烧出来用于清洗的灰。

items.example: Alkali was the older noun for these substances.
items.exampleCN: alkali 是这些物质的较早名词。

items.structure: adjective ending meaning 'of the nature of'
items.example: The ending turns the noun into a label for a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成性质标签。

items.meaning: having the character of an alkali
items.example: The soil here is alkaline.
items.exampleCN: 这里的土壤是碱性的。

items.example: The alkalinity of the water was measured.
items.exampleCN: 水的碱度被测量了。

items.example: The treatment alkalizes the waste stream.
items.exampleCN: 该处理使废液流碱化。

items.example: The additive alkalinizes the boiler water.
items.exampleCN: 这种添加剂使锅炉水碱化。

items.structure: alkali plus a medical state ending
items.meaning: a condition of excess base in the blood
items.example: The patient was treated for alkalosis.
items.exampleCN: 病人因碱中毒接受了治疗。

derivatives.zh: 由 alkaline 加性质词尾构成，义为「碱性；碱度」
基础名词，义为「碱；可溶性碱」
由 alkali 加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」
由 alkali 加医学病态词尾构成，义为「碱中毒」

definition_zh: 碱性；碱度；（水的）总碱度（抵偿酸的能力）
definition_en: the quality or degree of being alkaline, or the measured capacity of water to neutralise acid
core_image: 一只水样瓶旁摆着滴定管与色卡，滴到颜色定住的那一刻，读数才被写下
scene: 检测员把酸液滴进水样，直到颜色停住不动，然后写下这口井的碱度。The alkalinity of the well water was tested before the fish ponds were stocked.
sceneCN: 这里 alkalinity 指水呈碱性、能抵偿酸的程度（第 2 个义项：水的总碱度）；句意：在鱼塘放养之前，先测了这口井水的碱度。图中可辨识物件：水样瓶、滴定管、比色卡、记录表。

derivatives.zh: 由 alkali 加形容词词尾构成，义为「碱性的」
由 alkali 加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」
由 alkali 加医学病态词尾构成，义为「碱中毒」
由 alkali 加表示测量的成分构成，义为「碱度计」

senses.title: The quality of being alkaline
senses.definition: the character a substance has when it behaves as a base rather than an acid
senses.definitionCN: 某物质表现为碱而非酸时所具有的性质
senses.example: Farmers judge the alkalinity of the soil before choosing a crop.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在选择作物之前先判断土壤的碱性。
senses.why: The noun is the quality form of the adjective, so its first sense is simply the state of being alkaline.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是形容词的性质形式，因此第一个义项就是「呈碱性」这一状态。

senses.title: Water's capacity to absorb acid
senses.definition: the measured ability of water to neutralise added acid without a large change in pH, supplied mainly by carbonate and bicarbonate
senses.definitionCN: 水在加入酸后不使酸碱度大幅变化的能力，主要来自碳酸盐与碳酸氢盐
senses.example: The alkalinity of the well water was tested before the fish ponds were stocked.
senses.exampleCN: 在鱼塘放养之前，先测了这口井水的碱度。
senses.why: Water engineers care less about the label than about how much acid the water can swallow, so the noun became a capacity.
senses.whyCN: 水处理工程师关心的不只是标签，而是水能吞下多少酸，于是这个名词变成了一种能力。

senses.title: The basic condition of soil
senses.definition: the degree to which soil is basic, which controls nutrient availability and which crops can be grown
senses.definitionCN: 土壤偏碱的程度，决定养分有效性以及能种哪些作物
senses.example: High alkalinity locked iron out of reach of the plants.
senses.exampleCN: 高碱度使铁无法被植物吸收。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the measured sense to land, where the number predicts what will flourish.
senses.whyCN: 农业把可测量的义项用在土地上，那里的数字能预示什么会长得好。

senses.title: The sea's built-in buffer
senses.definition: the capacity of seawater to resist changes in pH, which keeps marine life stable
senses.definitionCN: 海水抵抗酸碱度变化的能力，使海洋生物得以稳定生存
senses.example: Decades of measurement show the ocean's alkalinity slowly shifting.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年测量显示海洋的碱度正在缓慢变化。
senses.why: Oceanography treats the capacity as a global property, because the buffer is what keeps a whole ecosystem from swinging.
senses.whyCN: 海洋学把这种能力当作全球尺度上的性质，因为正是这层缓冲让整个生态系统免于剧烈摆动。

senses.title: The number from a titration
senses.definition: the figure obtained by adding acid of known strength until the sample reaches a chosen end point
senses.definitionCN: 加入已知强度的酸直到样品到达选定终点所得到的数值
senses.example: The alkalinity test gave a value of two hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 碱度测定给出两百这个数值。
senses.why: Because the capacity can be spent exactly by a measured acid, it can be reported as a number in a logbook.
senses.whyCN: 既然这种能力可以被已知量的酸正好用掉，它就能作为数字记进记录本。

senses.title: A control target in pools and boilers
senses.titleCN: 水池与锅炉里的控制指标
senses.definition: the level of alkalinity kept within a set range so that equipment is protected and treatment works
senses.definitionCN: 为使设备受保护、处理生效而维持在设定范围内的碱度水平
senses.example: The operator raised the alkalinity to stop the pipes corroding.
senses.exampleCN: 操作员提高碱度以阻止管道腐蚀。
senses.why: Industry turns the measurement into a dial to be held steady, so the noun names a target rather than a natural fact.
senses.whyCN: 工业把测量变成一个要稳定握住的旋钮，于是这个名词命名一个目标，而非自然事实。

senses.title: A feature of lakes and streams
senses.definition: the basic character of a freshwater body, which shapes which species can live there
senses.definitionCN: 淡水水体的碱性格，决定哪些物种能生存
senses.example: The alkalinity of the stream fell after the mine opened.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场开工后，溪水的碱度下降了。
senses.why: Field surveys use the word as a lasting trait of a place, not a single reading.
senses.whyCN: 野外调查把这个词当作某地持久的特点，而不是一次读数。

senses.title: The opposite side of the acid measure
senses.definition: the mirror quantity to acidity, describing how far a solution leans toward base
senses.definitionCN: 与酸度相对的镜像量，描述溶液偏向碱的程度
senses.example: Chemists reported both acidity and alkalinity for the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家为样品同时报告了酸度与碱度。
senses.why: The two nouns divide the same scale between them, so each names the distance from neutral in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这两个名词把同一条尺度分成两半，各自命名从中性朝一个方向走出的距离。

intro.en: Alkalinity is alkali plus a quality ending, formed in the eighteenth century as chemistry needed a noun for the measured property. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: alkalinity 是 alkali 加性质名词词尾构成，出现于 18 世纪，当时化学需要一个名词来指这一可测量的性质。年代为约数。

items.en: The root is Arabic al-qily, the ashes of a salt-tolerant plant burned to make a cleansing substance.
items.cn: 词根是阿拉伯语 al-qily，指一种耐盐植物烧成的灰，用于制作清洗物质。

items.en: Medieval Latin adopted the term for the soda and potash substances that early chemists handled.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入该词，指早期化学家处理的苏打与碳酸钾类物质。

items.en: English took alkali in the seventeenth century, and the adjective alkaline followed in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 alkali，形容词 alkaline 于 18 世纪随后出现。

items.en: The quality noun added an ending that turns an adjective into a measurable state, so the word could enter titration records.
items.cn: 性质名词加上一个把形容词变成可测状态的词尾，于是这个词得以进入滴定记录。

items.en: Water treatment, pool care and boiler operation turned the measurement into a controlled target in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 水处理、泳池维护与锅炉运行在 20 世纪把这项测量变成受控指标。

items.en: Source uncertain for details: the exact plant behind the Arabic root is not securely established, and the noun's earliest English citation is not fixed either.
items.cn: 细节来源不确定：词根所指的确切阿拉伯植物未被牢固确立，该名词最早的英语引文同样未被固定。

note.en: The first group shares the alkali stem and differs by word class; the second group is the opposite measure and the instruments around it.
note.cn: 第一组共享 alkali 词干而词类不同；第二组是相对的度量与周围的仪器。

entries.definition: Having a pH above seven; it labels a substance, while alkalinity measures how strongly it does so.
entries.definitionCN: 酸碱度高于七；它给物质贴标签，而 alkalinity 测量其程度。

entries.definition: A soluble base; it is a thing, not a measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 可溶性碱；它是物质，不是度量。

entries.definition: To make something alkaline; it names an action, while the noun names a state.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变碱；它命名动作，而名词命名状态。

entries.definition: The titration that produces the number; here the noun is a modifier inside the name of a method.
entries.definitionCN: 产生该数值的滴定；这里该名词是方法名称里的修饰成分。

entries.definition: The measured degree of being acid; it points the other way along the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 所测的呈酸程度；它在同一条尺度上指向另一端。

entries.definition: The number of protons a base can accept, or the number of replaceable hydrogens in an acid; it counts capacity per molecule, not water's buffering.
entries.definitionCN: 一个碱能接受的质子数，或一种酸中可被置换的氢原子数；它按分子计数，而不是水的缓冲能力。

entries.definition: The resistance of a solution to pH change; alkalinity is one source of it, but the word names the behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 溶液抵抗酸碱度变化的能力；碱度是其来源之一，但这个词命名的是行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: alkaline plus the quality ending: the measured state of being basic.
normal.cn: alkaline 加性质词尾：呈碱这一可测状态。

normal.en: The family runs alkali, alkaline, alkalinity, alkalize, alkalosis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 alkali、alkaline、alkalinity、alkalize、alkalosis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the water side: total alkalinity, water alkalinity, alkalinity test.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出与水有关的一面：总碱度、水的碱度、碱度测定。

normal.en: Water engineers treat it as how much acid the water can swallow.
normal.cn: 水处理工程师把它看作「水能吞下多少酸」。

normal.en: Acidity and alkalinity divide the same scale at the neutral point.
normal.cn: 酸度与碱度在中性点把同一条尺度分成两半。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge that soaks up spilled vinegar without letting the puddle spread.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵吸掉泼出的醋，不让水洼扩大。

abstract.en: Picture a lake that keeps its mood steady while rain of different kinds falls on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湖，各种雨水落进去，它的脾气却保持稳定。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge the operator watches and turns until the needle sits in the safe band.
abstract.cn: 想象操作员盯着一个表盘，把指针调进安全的那一段。

examples.en: The lab reports total alkalinity alongside pH for every sample.
examples.cn: 实验室为每个样品同时报告总碱度与酸碱度。

examples.en: Low alkalinity made the stream vulnerable to acid rain.
examples.cn: 低碱度使这条溪流容易受酸雨影响。

examples.en: Operators check alkalinity twice a day in the cooling tower.
examples.cn: 操作员每天在冷却塔检查碱度两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「alkaline（碱性）+ ity（程度）」——碱的程度，就是碱度

root: 阿拉伯 al-qily「盐生植物的灰」→ 中世纪拉丁 alkali → 英语 alkali、alkaline + 表示性质的名词词尾；指碱性或可测的总碱度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one basic capacity: the quality itself, water's ability to absorb acid, the soil verdict, the sea's buffer, the titration number, an industrial target, a whole stream, and the mirror half of the acid scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种碱的能力：性质本身、水抵偿酸的能力、土壤判断、海洋缓冲、滴定数值、工业指标、整条溪流，以及酸度尺度上的镜像那一半。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: acid dripped into a sample until the colour holds, and only then is the figure written.
core.cn: 核心意象：酸滴进样品，直到颜色定住，这时才写下数字。

branches.en: THE QUALITY AND ITS MIRROR: the state of being basic, and the half of the scale that faces acidity.
branches.cn: 性质及其镜像：呈碱的状态，以及尺度上与酸度相对的那一半。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND NUMBER: how much acid the water can take, and the figure a titration writes down.
branches.cn: 能力与数字：水能承受多少酸，以及滴定写下的数值。

branches.en: THE LAND: the same capacity decides which nutrients stay reachable in a field.
branches.cn: 土地：同一种能力决定田里哪些养分仍可被够到。

branches.en: THE WIDE WATER: a sea and a stream both hold a basic character that keeps life steady.
branches.cn: 广阔的水：海与溪都保有碱的性格，使生命保持稳定。

branches.en: THE DIAL: in a plant the capacity becomes a range that must be held, not merely observed.
branches.cn: 表盘：在工厂里，这种能力变成一个必须维持的范围，而不只是被观察。

intro.en: Alkalinity is an Arabic-derived noun plus a quality ending, and the family covers chemistry, water treatment and medicine.
intro.cn: alkalinity 是一个阿拉伯语来源的名词加性质词尾，词族覆盖化学、水处理与医学。

latinIntro.en: The root is Arabic and reached Europe through medieval Latin; Latin supplies only the endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自阿拉伯语，经中世纪拉丁语传入欧洲；拉丁语只提供词尾，因此不列词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The root names the ashes used for cleansing.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名用于清洗的灰。

items.example: Alkali is the older noun.
items.exampleCN: alkali 是较早的名词。

items.meaning: having the character of an alkali
items.example: The water is alkaline.
items.exampleCN: 这水是碱性的。

items.structure: noun ending for state or quality
items.example: The ending makes the property measurable.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使该性质可被测量。

items.meaning: the measured state of being basic
items.example: Total alkalinity was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 总碱度被记录了下来。

items.example: The reagent alkalizes the solution.
items.exampleCN: 该试剂使溶液碱化。

items.structure: alkali plus a medical state ending
items.example: Alkalosis can follow prolonged vomiting.
items.exampleCN: 长时间呕吐后可能出现碱中毒。

items.example: The alkalimeter replaced the older titration.
items.exampleCN: 碱度计取代了较早的滴定法。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「碱性的」
基础名词，义为「碱」
由基础名词加使动词尾构成，义为「使碱化」

definition_zh: 酸碱度；pH 值（氢离子活度以十为底的负对数）
definition_en: a number expressing the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, equal to the negative logarithm of its hydrogen ion activity
core_image: 一支细玻璃探头插进样杯，屏幕上的数字停在一个小数，旁边摆着一排比色纸
scene: 检测员把探头伸进溪水，屏幕停在一个小数，随后才把水样送回实验室。A meter dipped into the stream reports the pH before the sample is sent to the lab.
sceneCN: 这里 pH 指表示溶液酸碱程度的数值（第 1 个义项：酸碱度这一读数值）；句意：伸入溪水的仪表在水样送检之前就报出了酸碱度。图中可辨识物件：玻璃探头、读数屏、样杯、比色纸。

derivatives.zh: 由 pH 与表示仪器的名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度计」
由 pH 与表示标度的名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度标度」
按同一构词法把氢换成氢氧根所得，义为「氢氧根指数」

senses.title: The reading itself
senses.definition: the number that reports how acid or basic a solution is
senses.definitionCN: 报告溶液酸碱程度的那个数字
senses.example: A meter dipped into the stream reports the pH before the sample is sent to the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 伸入溪水的仪表在水样送检之前就报出了酸碱度。
senses.why: The symbol is a shorthand label for a single number, so the most common sense is simply the value one reads or hears.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号是一个数字的简写标签，因此最常见的义项就是人们读到或听到的那个值。

senses.title: The negative logarithm of hydrogen activity
senses.definition: the formal definition: minus the base-ten logarithm of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
senses.definitionCN: 正式定义：溶液中氢离子活度以十为底的对数取负
senses.example: Each unit of pH stands for a tenfold change in hydrogen ion activity.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个 pH 单位代表氢离子活度十倍的变化。
senses.why: Because the numbers span many powers of ten, a logarithmic scale was chosen, and the symbol encodes that power.
senses.whyCN: 由于数值跨越许多个十的幂，人们选用对数尺度，而这个符号正编码了那个幂。

senses.title: A property of a particular solution
senses.definition: the acid or basic character of a named liquid, as in the pH of milk or of rain
senses.definitionCN: 某种指定液体的酸碱性格，如牛奶或雨水的 pH
senses.example: The pH of the milk fell as the bacteria grew.
senses.exampleCN: 随着细菌繁殖，牛奶的酸碱度下降。
senses.why: The reading is always of something, so the symbol also names a property that a particular liquid possesses.
senses.whyCN: 读数总归是关于某物的，因此这个符号也命名某一具体液体所具有的属性。

senses.title: What an instrument displays
senses.definition: the figure shown by a meter or test strip, which stands for the solution's condition
senses.definitionCN: 由仪表或试纸显示的数字，代表溶液的状况
senses.example: The meter's pH drifted until the probe was recalibrated.
senses.exampleCN: 在探头重新校准之前，仪表的酸碱度读数一直漂移。
senses.why: In practice people meet the value through a device, so the symbol is used for the display as well as for the chemical fact.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中人们通过器件遇到这个值，因此该符号既指化学事实，也指显示结果。

senses.title: A position on a numbered scale
senses.definition: a place on the conventional scale that runs from strongly acid to strongly basic, with seven as neutral
senses.definitionCN: 在从强酸到强碱的惯用尺度上的位置，以七为中性
senses.example: The scale usually runs from zero to fourteen, though real solutions can fall outside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这一尺度通常从零到十四，但实际溶液也可能落在其外。
senses.why: Because the readings are ordered, the word also names the axis itself, and people speak of being low or high on it.
senses.whyCN: 由于读数是排序的，这个词也命名那条轴本身，人们会说在轴上偏低或偏高。

senses.title: The balance of a living body
senses.definition: the tightly controlled acid-base level of blood or other body fluid, kept within a narrow range
senses.definitionCN: 血液或其他体液中受严格控制、维持在窄范围内的酸碱水平
senses.example: Doctors watch the pH of the blood during long surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间手术中医生会监测血液的酸碱度。
senses.why: Physiology applies the reading to a body that must hold it steady, so the number becomes a vital sign.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个读数用在一个必须维持稳定的身体上，于是这个数字变成一项生命体征。

senses.title: The condition of soil or water
senses.definition: the acid-base level of soil, rain, a lake or the sea, which shapes what can live there
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、雨水、湖泊或海洋的酸碱水平，决定那里能生存什么
senses.example: Soil pH decides whether the blueberries will thrive.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤酸碱度决定蓝莓能否长好。
senses.why: Environmental science uses the symbol as a property of places, where it acts as a long-lasting setting.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把这个符号当作地点的属性，在那里它起长期背景的作用。

senses.title: A quantity to be adjusted
senses.definition: a controlled parameter that operators raise or lower by adding acid or base
senses.definitionCN: 操作者通过加酸或加碱来升高或降低的受控参数
senses.example: The plant adjusts the pH of the waste stream before releasing it.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂在排放前调节废液的酸碱度。
senses.why: Once the value can be measured and changed, it becomes a dial in a process rather than a mere observation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个值可以被测量并改变，它就变成流程中的一个旋钮，而不只是观察对象。

intro.en: pH was coined in 1909 by the Danish chemist Søren Sørensen as a compact notation for hydrogen ion power. Its parts are German and Greek rather than Latin.
intro.cn: pH 由丹麦化学家瑟伦森于 1909 年造出，作为「氢离子幂」的紧凑记号；其部件来自德语与希腊语，而非拉丁语。

items.en: Hydrogen goes back to Greek hydor 'water' plus -genes 'born', a name given to the gas because burning it produced water.
items.cn: hydrogen 上溯到希腊语 hydor「水」加 -genes「产生」，这个名称给该气体，是因为它燃烧时生成水。

items.en: French chemists named the gas hydrogène at the end of the eighteenth century, and English adopted hydrogen soon after.
items.cn: 法国化学家在 18 世纪末把该气体命名为 hydrogène，英语随后采用 hydrogen。

items.en: Sørensen took p from the German word for 'power', so the first element of the symbol stands for the exponent rather than for a quantity itself.
items.cn: 瑟伦森取德语中表示「幂」的词首字母，因此符号的第一个成分代表指数，而不是某个量本身。

items.en: Working on the acidity of solutions, Sørensen introduced the notation for the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration, and the compact symbol spread at once.
items.cn: 瑟伦森在研究溶液的酸度时，为氢离子浓度的负对数引入这一记号，这个紧凑符号迅速传开。

items.en: Medicine, agriculture, water treatment and industry adopted the symbol in the following decades, each adding its own standard range.
items.cn: 医学、农业、水处理与工业在此后数十年采用该符号，各自加上自己的标准范围。

items.en: Source uncertain for one detail: the exact reasoning behind the letter p has been explained in more than one way; the German Potenz 'power' account is the most widely accepted, while Latin pondus 'weight' and French puissance have also been proposed, so no single reading is settled.
items.cn: 有一处细节来源不确定：字母 p 的确切由来曾有不止一种解释；德语 Potenz「幂」之说最为流行，也有人提出拉丁语 pondus「重量」与法语 puissance，因此并无单一结论被视为定论。

note.en: The first group is built with the same symbol pattern or names the instruments; the second group holds the quantities the symbol reports.
note.cn: 第一组用同一符号模式构成，或命名相关仪器；第二组是该符号所报告的各个量。

entries.definition: The same construction applied to hydroxide ion activity; it reports the basic side of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 对氢氧根离子活度施用同一构词法；它报告同一尺度的碱性一侧。

entries.definition: The device that reads the value; the symbol is a modifier inside the name of the tool.
entries.definitionCN: 读取该值的装置；符号是工具名称里的修饰成分。

entries.definition: The ordered range of readings; the symbol names the quantity, the compound names the ruler it sits on.
entries.definitionCN: 读数的有序范围；符号命名量，复合词命名它所依附的标尺。

entries.definition: A paper treated with dyes that change colour at different values; it displays the reading without electronics.
entries.definitionCN: 浸过染料、在不同数值下变色的纸；不用电子器件就能显示读数。

entries.definition: The measured degree of being acid; pH is one standard way of reporting that degree.
entries.definitionCN: 所测的呈酸程度；pH 是报告该程度的一种标准方式。

entries.definition: The degree of being basic, or water's capacity to absorb acid; related to pH but not the same measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 呈碱的程度，或水抵偿酸的能力；与 pH 相关，但不是同一种测量。

entries.definition: The amount of free hydrogen ions per volume; pH is its negative logarithm, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 单位体积内自由氢离子的量；pH 是该量的负对数，而不是量本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The p stands for the German word for power, and the H stands for hydrogen.
normal.cn: 字母 p 代表德语中表示「幂」的词，字母 H 代表氢。

normal.en: Every unit is a tenfold change in hydrogen ion activity, which is why the scale is logarithmic.
normal.cn: 每一个单位都是氢离子活度的十倍变化，这就是尺度取对数的原因。

normal.en: Fixed compounds mark the tools: pH meter, pH scale, pH paper.
normal.cn: 固定复合词标出工具：酸碱度计、酸碱度标度、酸碱度试纸。

normal.en: The neutral point is seven, and both directions run away from it.
normal.cn: 中性点是七，两个方向都从中性点向外延伸。

normal.en: Sørensen introduced the notation in 1909 while studying solution acidity.
normal.cn: 瑟伦森在 1909 年研究溶液酸度时引入了这一记号。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks get ten times farther apart at every step.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，每走一格，刻度间距就变成十倍。

abstract.en: Picture a single drop of colour spreading through a whole glass of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴颜色在一整杯水里慢慢散开。

abstract.en: Picture a dial in a plant room that someone turns until the needle sits in the green band.
abstract.cn: 想象厂房里一个表盘，有人转动它，直到指针落在绿色区段。

examples.en: Rain in the region often has a pH below five.
examples.cn: 该地区的雨水酸碱度常低于五。

examples.en: The technician calibrated the pH meter before sampling.
examples.cn: 技术员在取样前校准了酸碱度计。

examples.en: Buffers keep the pH steady when acid is added.
examples.cn: 加入酸时，缓冲体系使酸碱度保持稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「p（幂）+ H（氢）」——氢离子幂的缩写，就是酸碱度

root: 1909 年瑟伦森所造的记号：p 取自德语中表示「幂」的词，H 代表氢；氢一词出自希腊语 hydor「水」+ -genes「产生」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one logarithmic reading: the number itself, its formal definition, a property of a liquid, an instrument display, a position on the scale, a body's balance, a landscape's condition, and a parameter to adjust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个对数读数：数字本身、其正式定义、某液体的属性、仪器显示、尺度上的位置、身体的平衡、景观的状况，以及可调节的参数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a probe in a cup, a decimal frozen on the screen, and a row of colour strips beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：探头插在杯里，屏幕上停着一个小数，旁边摆着一排比色纸。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND ITS OWNER: the reading, and the particular liquid whose condition it reports.
branches.cn: 数字及其所属：读数，以及它所报告状况的那种液体。

branches.en: THE LOGARITHM: behind the number lies a power of ten, which is what makes the scale compress huge ranges.
branches.cn: 对数：数字背后是一个十的幂，正是它让尺度压缩了巨大的范围。

branches.en: THE DISPLAY: in daily work the value arrives through a device, so the symbol stands for what the screen shows.
branches.cn: 显示：在日常工作里，这个值通过器件抵达，于是符号代指屏幕所示。

branches.en: THE AXIS AND THE PLACE: the ordered scale, and the condition of a field, a lake or a sea upon it.
branches.cn: 轴与位置：有序的尺度，以及田、湖或海在这条轴上的状况。

branches.en: THE LIVING AND THE CONTROLLED: a body holds the number within a narrow band, while a plant turns it like a dial.
branches.cn: 生命与受控：身体把数字守在窄带内，而工厂把它当作旋钮来转。

intro.en: pH is a two-letter notation rather than a word with affixes, and each letter stands for a different source.
intro.cn: pH 不是带词缀的单词，而是一个两字母记号，每个字母各自代表不同的来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin plays no part in this symbol: the first element is German and the second goes back through French to Greek, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这个符号里没有角色：第一个成分来自德语，第二个经法语上溯希腊语，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.example: The notation fits on a dial or a label.
items.exampleCN: 这个记号可以印在表盘或标签上。

items.structure: abbreviation of the German word for power
items.example: The letter marks the exponent, not the amount.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母标的是指数，而非数量。

items.example: The second letter names the ion being counted.
items.exampleCN: 第二个字母命名被计数的离子。

items.structure: French hydrogène, from Greek words for water and born
items.meaning: the gas that makes water when burned
items.meaningCN: 燃烧时生成水的那种气体
items.example: Hydrogen was named for the water it produces.
items.exampleCN: 氢因其生成的水而得名。

items.example: The reading tracks the activity of the hydron.
items.exampleCN: 这个读数追踪裸氢离子的活度。

items.structure: the notation plus the word for a graduated range
items.example: Seven sits at the middle of the pH scale.
items.exampleCN: 七位于酸碱度标度的中间。

items.structure: the notation plus the word for an instrument
items.meaning: a device that reads the value
items.example: The pH meter needs calibration each morning.
items.exampleCN: 酸碱度计每天早上都要校准。

items.structure: the notation plus the word for a strip
items.example: The pH paper turned green in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 试纸在样品里变成了绿色。

derivatives.zh: 由 pH 与仪器名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度计」
由 pH 与标度名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度标度」
按同一构词法把氢换成氢氧根所得，义为「氢氧根指数」

definition_zh: 中和；中和作用；抵消；使失效；（语音）中和
definition_en: the process of making something neutral, especially the reaction in which an acid and a base cancel each other and form a salt
core_image: 两只烧杯并排，一杯泛红一杯泛蓝，倒进同一个容器后颜色退成平淡的浅色
scene: 实验台上把泛红的酸液倒进泛蓝的碱液，颜色退掉，杯壁摸起来只是温热。Neutralization in the beaker leaves a warm salty solution and a flat reading.
sceneCN: 这里 neutralization 指酸与碱相互抵消、生成盐和水的过程（第 1 个义项：酸碱中和）；句意：烧杯里的中和留下温热的盐溶液与一个平缓的读数。图中可辨识物件：两只烧杯、退去的颜色、温度计、记录纸。

pos.zh: 中和；中和作用；抵消；使失效

forms.label: 复数（指多次或多种中和）

derivatives.zh: 由 neutral 加使动词尾构成，义为「使中和、使失效」
由 neutralize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已中和的」
由 neutral 加状态名词词尾构成，义为「中立；中性」
由 neutralize 加施动词尾构成，义为「中和剂」

senses.title: Acid and base cancelling out
senses.definition: the reaction in which hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions combine, so that an acid and a base stop being acid and base
senses.definitionCN: 氢离子与氢氧根离子结合，使酸不再呈酸、碱不再呈碱的反应
senses.example: Neutralization in the beaker leaves a warm salty solution and a flat reading.
senses.exampleCN: 烧杯里的中和留下温热的盐溶液与一个平缓的读数。
senses.why: The noun says the result is neither one thing nor the other, which is exactly what the word for 'neither' meant in Latin.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词说明结果是既非此也非彼，而这正是它在拉丁语里那个「两者皆非」的词所表达的意思。

senses.title: Making a substance neutral
senses.definition: the act of bringing a solution to a neutral condition, neither acid nor basic
senses.definitionCN: 把溶液带到既非酸也非碱的中性状态的行为
senses.example: Complete neutralization is needed before the sample can be discarded.
senses.exampleCN: 样品丢弃前需要完全中和。
senses.why: The reaction is often an aim rather than an event, so the noun can name the deliberate achievement of neutrality.
senses.whyCN: 这一反应常常是一个目标而非自然发生的事，因此这个名词也可以指有意达到中性的结果。

senses.title: Cancelling an effect or influence
senses.definition: the removal of the force of something by an opposing force, so that neither prevails
senses.definitionCN: 用相反的力量消除某物的作用，使任何一方都不占上风
senses.example: The neutralization of the two campaigns left the voters undecided.
senses.exampleCN: 两场宣传相互抵消，选民依然拿不定主意。
senses.why: The chemical picture of two forces cancelling is borrowed for politics and argument, where no balance sheet is involved.
senses.whyCN: 化学上两股力量相消的图景被借到政治与论辩里，那里并没有化学方程式。

senses.title: Putting a target out of action
senses.definition: the military act of destroying or disabling a target so that it can no longer function
senses.definitionCN: 摧毁或使目标瘫痪、使其无法继续运作的军事行动
senses.example: The report described the neutralization of the launch site.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了对该发射场实施的压制。
senses.why: Military writing uses the euphemistic sense: the target is made harmless, as an acid is made harmless by a base.
senses.whyCN: 军事写作使用这一委婉义：目标被弄得无害，正如酸被碱弄得无害。

senses.title: Taking the power out of a poison
senses.definition: the process of making a toxin or venom harmless by binding or counteracting it
senses.definitionCN: 通过结合或对抗使毒素或毒液变得无害的过程
senses.example: Antivenom works by neutralization of the venom proteins.
senses.exampleCN: 抗蛇毒血清通过中和毒液蛋白起作用。
senses.why: Medicine applies the cancelling image to poisons, where the hostile force is a molecule rather than an army.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这种「相消」图景用在毒物上，那里敌对的力量是分子而不是军队。

senses.title: A distinction disappearing in speech
senses.titleCN: 语言中某个对立的消失
senses.definition: the loss of a contrast between two speech sounds in a particular position, so that they no longer distinguish words
senses.definitionCN: 两个语音在特定位置上失去对立，因而不再区分词义
senses.example: Neutralization of the two vowels occurs at the end of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个元音在词尾发生了中和。
senses.why: Linguistics borrows the word for a contrast that stops mattering, which mirrors a chemical cancellation without any chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借这个词指一种不再起作用的对立，这与化学上的相消相映，却不涉及任何化学。

senses.title: Making a place or state neutral
senses.definition: the act of declaring a country, zone or institution neutral and free from involvement in a conflict
senses.definitionCN: 宣布某国、某区域或某机构中立、不卷入冲突的行为
senses.example: The neutralization of the border zone was written into the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 边境地带的中立化被写进了条约。
senses.why: Diplomacy takes the adjective 'neutral' in its political sense and adds the action ending, so the word means making someone stand aside.
senses.whyCN: 外交把形容词「中立」的政治义加上动作词尾，于是这个词指使某方站到一边。

senses.title: Balancing a waste stream
senses.definition: the industrial step of adding acid or base to waste so that it can be safely released
senses.definitionCN: 向废液中加酸或加碱、使其可安全排放的工业步骤
senses.example: Wastewater neutralization is the last step before discharge.
senses.exampleCN: 废水的中和是排放前的最后一步。
senses.why: Industry makes the reaction routine, so the noun names a fixed stage in a treatment line.
senses.whyCN: 工业把这一反应变成常规操作，于是这个名词命名处理流程中一个固定的阶段。

intro.en: Neutralization is built on neutral, which comes from Latin neuter 'neither of the two', plus an action ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neutralization 由 neutral 加动作名词词尾构成，而 neutral 来自拉丁 neuter「两者皆非」。年代为约数。

items.en: Neuter was formed from ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of the two', so it meant 'neither one' from the start.
items.cn: neuter 由 ne-「不」加 uter「两者之一」构成，因此从一开始就是「哪一个都不是」。

items.en: The adjective neutralis described something belonging to neither side, used of grammar and of parties in a dispute.
items.cn: 形容词 neutralis 描述不属于任何一方的事物，用于语法，也用于争端中的各方。

items.en: French neutral and English neutral carried the idea of standing aside, and the verb neutralize added the action of putting something into that position.
items.cn: 法语与英语中的 neutral 承载「站到一边」的意思，动词 neutralize 则加上「把某物放到那个位置」的动作。

items.en: Eighteenth-century chemistry used the image for an acid and a base that leave neither character behind, and the noun named that result.
items.cn: 18 世纪化学用这个图景指酸与碱互相抵消、不留任何一方性格，名词则命名这一结果。

items.en: Politics, medicine and linguistics borrowed the same picture: a force, a poison or a contrast is made to stop mattering.
items.cn: 政治、医学与语言学借用同一图景：让某种力量、毒物或对立不再起作用。

items.en: First date uncertain: the noun is recorded from the eighteenth century, but the precise year of its first chemical use is not securely fixed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个名词在 18 世纪已有记录，但其首次用于化学的确切年份并未被牢固确定。

note.en: The first group shares the neutral stem and differs by word class; the second group holds neighbouring chemical and figurative ways of cancelling something.
note.cn: 第一组共享 neutral 词干而词类不同；第二组是相邻的「抵消某物」的化学与比喻说法。

entries.definition: To make something neutral or harmless; the noun names the event, while the verb names the act of bringing it about.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物中性或无害；名词命名事件，动词命名促成该事件的动作。

entries.definition: Neither acid nor basic, or taking no side in a dispute; it describes a state, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 既非酸也非碱，或在争端中不站边；它描述状态，不描述过程。

entries.definition: The condition of being neutral, especially in politics; it is a lasting position rather than an action performed.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中立的状况，尤指政治上；它是持久立场，而不是被执行的行动。

entries.definition: A substance or device that performs the neutralization; it names the doer of the act.
entries.definitionCN: 执行中和的物质或装置；它命名动作的执行者。

entries.definition: A procedure that adds measured amounts until the reaction is complete; neutralization can be its aim, but titration adds the measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步加入定量试剂直到反应完成的操作；中和可以是其目的，而滴定另有测量之意。

entries.definition: The removal of one effect by an opposite one; it is the plain-language counterpart of the figurative senses of neutralization.
entries.definitionCN: 用相反的作用消除某一效果；它是中和的比喻义在日常语言里的对应说法。

entries.definition: A system that resists pH change instead of removing the acid entirely; buffering and neutralization work differently.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗酸碱度变化的体系，而不是彻底去除酸；缓冲与中和的作用方式不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: neuter meant 'neither of the two', so neutralization leaves neither an acid nor a base.
normal.cn: neuter 意为「两者皆非」，因此中和之后既不是酸也不是碱。

normal.en: The family runs neutral, neutralize, neutralized, neutrality, neutralization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 neutral、neutralize、neutralized、neutrality、neutralization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the lab side: acid-base neutralization, neutralization reaction, neutralization point.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出实验室的一面：酸碱中和、中和反应、中和点。

normal.en: The same picture covers armies, venoms and vowel contrasts.
normal.cn: 同一图景也适用于军队、毒液与元音对立。

normal.en: Waste treatment makes it the last step before discharge.
normal.cn: 废水处理把它变成排放前的最后一步。

abstract.en: Picture two coloured liquids meeting and the colour simply going out of both.
abstract.cn: 想象两种带色的液体相遇，颜色从两边一起退掉。

abstract.en: Picture two people pushing a door from opposite sides so that it does not move.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人从两边推同一扇门，门纹丝不动。

abstract.en: Picture two voices arguing until both fall silent at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人争辩，直到同一刻双双沉默。

examples.en: The lab worksheet asks for the heat released by neutralization.
examples.cn: 实验单要求记录中和所放出的热。

examples.en: Neutralization of the soil improved the pasture within two seasons.
examples.cn: 土壤中和之后，牧草在两个季节内改善。

examples.en: The treaty provided for neutralization of the canal zone.
examples.cn: 条约规定对运河区实行中立化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「neutral（中性）+ ization（化）」——把两边都化掉，就是中和

root: 拉丁 neuter「两者皆非」= ne-（不）+ uter（两者之一）→ neutral + 动作名词词尾；指使酸与碱都失去性格、达到中性。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cancellation: acid meets base, a liquid is brought to neutral, two campaigns cancel, a target is disabled, a poison is made harmless, a sound contrast vanishes, a zone is declared neutral, and waste is balanced before release.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种相消：酸遇碱、液体被带到中性、两场宣传互相抵消、目标被压制、毒物变无害、语音对立消失、区域被宣布中立、废液在排放前被调平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red and blue liquids poured together until both colours die into a pale, unremarkable tone.
core.cn: 核心意象：红与蓝两种液体倒在一起，颜色都退成平淡的浅色。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL CORE: the two opposites cancel, and the aim is a liquid that is neither one.
branches.cn: 化学核心：两种相反之物相消，目标是得到既非此也非彼的液体。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL PICTURE: two campaigns cancel each other, and a zone is put outside the conflict.
branches.cn: 政治图景：两场宣传互相抵消，一片区域被放到冲突之外。

branches.en: THE MILITARY EUPHEMISM: the hostile thing is made unable to act, as if it had met its opposite.
branches.cn: 军事委婉语：敌对之物被弄得无法行动，仿佛遇到了它的反面。

branches.en: THE MEDICAL USE: a poison is bound and stripped of its power.
branches.cn: 医学用法：毒物被结合住，力量被剥掉。

branches.en: THE QUIET FORMS: a vowel contrast stops distinguishing words, and a waste stream is brought to the middle before release.
branches.cn: 安静的形式：元音对立不再区分词义，废液在排放前被带回中间。

intro.en: Neutralization is a Latin adjective plus an action ending, and the stem also builds the political and grammatical words.
intro.cn: neutralization 是一个拉丁形容词加动作名词词尾，这个词干也构成政治与语法方面的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin neuter gives neutral, neutrality and neutralize, while the negative element behind it also appears in neither and never.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 neuter 衍生 neutral、neutrality 与 neutralize，而它背后的否定成分也出现在 neither 与 never 中。

items.example: The negative element denies both alternatives.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定成分把两个选项都否定掉。

senses.title: A solid becoming part of a liquid
senses.titleCN: 固体成为液体的一部分
senses.definition: to pass into a liquid and become uniformly mixed with it, so that no separate solid remains
senses.definitionCN: 进入液体并与之均匀混合，不再有单独的固体留下
senses.example: Stir the sugar and it will dissolve before the water cools.
senses.exampleCN: 搅一搅，糖会在水凉之前就溶掉。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to loosen apart, which is exactly what happens to the ordered lattice of a solid as the liquid takes it up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本意是「松开、拆散」，而这正是液体的接纳使固体的有序结构所经历的事。

senses.title: Making a solid disappear into a liquid
senses.definition: to cause a solid to enter a liquid and mix with it
senses.definitionCN: 使固体进入液体并与之混合
senses.example: Dissolve the powder in a litre of warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 把粉末溶进一升温水中。
senses.why: The same loosening event is viewed with a doer, giving the transitive pattern used in recipes and procedures.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「拆散」事件在带作用者时被观察，就得到菜谱与流程里所用的及物句式。

senses.title: An organization formally ending
senses.definition: to bring an assembly, company or partnership to an end and distribute what remains
senses.definitionCN: 使集会、公司或合伙关系终止并分配剩余之物
senses.example: The partners voted to dissolve the firm after thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 合伙人在三十年后投票决定解散公司。
senses.why: An organisation is held together by ties, so ending it is pictured as loosening those ties until the group no longer holds a shape.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠各种联结维持，因此终止它被想象成松开这些联结，直到群体不再成形。

senses.title: A marriage or contract ended
senses.definition: to bring a marriage, legal tie or agreement to a formal end
senses.definitionCN: 使婚姻、法律纽带或协议正式终止
senses.example: The court dissolved the agreement after the breach.
senses.exampleCN: 违约之后，法院解除了该协议。
senses.why: Law uses the loosening image for any binding tie, so a marriage ends in the same vocabulary as a company.
senses.whyCN: 法律把「松开」的图景用于任何有约束力的纽带，于是婚姻与公司的结束用同一套词。

senses.title: Fading away out of sight
senses.definition: to gradually disappear, as fog, a crowd or an image does
senses.definitionCN: 像雾、人群或影像那样逐渐消失
senses.example: The morning fog dissolved as the sun rose.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳升起时，晨雾散去了。
senses.why: What has no remaining shape has in a sense been loosened to nothing, so disappearance is described with the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 不再保有形状之物，某种意义上是被松开到无形，因此消失也用同一个动词描述。

senses.title: Losing control to tears or laughter
senses.definition: to give way completely to an emotion, so that composure disappears
senses.definitionCN: 完全让位给某种情绪，以致镇定消失
senses.example: She dissolved into laughter at the memory.
senses.exampleCN: 想起那件事，她忍不住大笑起来。
senses.why: Composure is a held shape; when it is loosened, the person 'melts' into the feeling, and the verb keeps its physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 镇定是一种维持着的形状；一旦松开，人就「融化」进那种情绪，动词保留着它的身体图景。

senses.title: Making doubts or barriers disappear
senses.definition: to remove a difficulty, suspicion or distance so that it no longer stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 消除困难、怀疑或距离，使其不再阻挡
senses.example: A single honest conversation dissolved their suspicion.
senses.exampleCN: 一次坦诚的交谈就消解了他们的怀疑。
senses.why: Abstract obstacles behave like solids: they can be made to lose their outline and stop blocking the way.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的障碍表现得像固体：可以让它失去轮廓，不再挡路。

senses.title: One film image melting into the next
senses.titleCN: 电影画面溶入下一个画面
senses.definition: to change from one shot to another by fading out and fading in at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 通过一边淡出一边淡入，从一个镜头转到另一个镜头
senses.example: The director dissolved from the street to the dream.
senses.exampleCN: 导演用叠化从街道转到梦境。
senses.why: The older image loses its edges while the newer one gains them, which looks exactly like one thing loosening into another.
senses.whyCN: 旧画面失去边缘，新画面同时取得边缘，看上去正像一物松开化成另一物。

senses.title: Water wearing away rock
senses.definition: to remove mineral material from rock by chemical action, often leaving cavities
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学作用把矿物从岩石中带走，常留下孔洞
senses.example: Groundwater dissolved the limestone into a network of caves.
senses.exampleCN: 地下水把石灰岩溶成一片洞穴网络。
senses.why: Geology applies the chemical loosening to stone over long periods, where the liquid slowly takes the solid apart.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把化学上的「松开」用在长时段的石头上，液体在那里慢慢把固体拆走。

intro.en: Dissolve comes from Latin dissolvere, 'to loosen apart', built on dis- 'apart' and solvere 'to loosen'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dissolve 来自拉丁 dissolvere「拆散、松开」，由 dis-「分开」与 solvere「松开」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, release', probably from se- 'apart' plus luere 'to loosen'; it is also the source of solve.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、释放」，一般认为由 se-「分开」加 luere「松开」构成；它也是 solve 的来源。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' strengthened the loosening, giving dissolvere 'to part the bonds of something, to break it up'.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加强了「松开」的意思，构成 dissolvere「拆开某物的联结、使之解体」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into English in the medieval period, first of loosening a bond and ending an arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语在中世纪把这个动词带入英语，最初指松开联结、终止安排。

items.en: The chemical sense of a solid passing into a liquid grew alongside alchemy and pharmacy, where substances were repeatedly loosened in liquids.
items.cn: 固体进入液体的化学义随着炼金术与制药发展起来，那里物质反复被液体松开。

items.en: Disappearance, emotional collapse and the cinema's fading transition all reuse the picture of a shape losing its edges.
items.cn: 消失、情绪失控与电影里的淡变过渡，都在重复「形状失去边缘」这一图景。

items.en: Reconstruction for one point: the older make-up of solvere is debated; the account with se- 'apart' and luere 'to loosen' is a widely accepted reconstruction rather than a demonstrated fact.
items.cn: 有一处属重构形式：solvere 更早的构成存在争论；一般认为由 se-「分开」加 luere「松开」构成，但这是流传较广的重构，并非已证实的事实。

note.en: The first group shares the solvere root and is frequently confused; the second group holds other ways a solid or a group can come apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享 solvere 词根，常被混淆；第二组是固体或群体分离的其他方式。

entries.definition: The process or result of dissolving or of ending an assembly; it names the event, not the act of bringing it about.
entries.definitionCN: 溶解的过程或结果，或集会的终止；它命名事件，而非促成事件的动作。

entries.definition: From the same Latin loosening word, but English uses it for finding an answer to a problem, with no liquid involved.
entries.definitionCN: 出自同一个表示「松开」的拉丁词，但英语用它指找出问题的答案，不涉及液体。

entries.definition: Ab- 'away' plus solvere: to release someone from a duty or a blame, a loosening of obligation rather than of matter.
entries.definitionCN: ab-「离开」加 solvere：把某人从义务或责难中释放，松开的是责任而非物质。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus solvere: to settle or decide something, pictured as loosening a knot until it comes apart.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再次」加 solvere：解决或决定某事，被想象成把结松开直到散开。

entries.definition: To change from solid to liquid through heat; dissolve needs a solvent, while melting needs only temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 因受热从固体变成液体；溶解需要溶剂，而熔化只需要温度。

entries.definition: To come apart or to end a group; it states the separation without the image of loosened bonds.
entries.definitionCN: 散开或结束一个群体；它直说分离，不带「松开联结」的图景。

entries.definition: To grow weaker or less visible; it describes the loss of brightness, while dissolve stresses loss of outline.
entries.definitionCN: 变弱或变得不那么可见；它描述亮度的丧失，而 dissolve 强调轮廓的消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' plus solvere 'loosen': to loosen a thing until it comes apart.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」加 solvere「松开」：把某物松到散开。

normal.en: The family runs dissolve, dissolution, dissolved, dissolving, dissolvable, dissolvent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dissolve、dissolution、dissolved、dissolving、dissolvable、dissolvent。

normal.en: Fixed phrases cover kitchen, law and feeling: dissolve in water, dissolve a partnership, dissolve into tears.
normal.cn: 固定搭配覆盖厨房、法律与情绪：溶于水、解除合伙、哭成泪人。

normal.en: The same root gives solve, resolve and absolve, each loosening something different.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 solve、resolve 与 absolve，各自松开不同的东西。

normal.en: Cinema borrowed the word because one image loses its edges as another gains them.
normal.cn: 电影借用了这个词，因为一个画面失去边缘时，另一个画面正取得边缘。

abstract.en: Picture a sugar cube shrinking at the edges until only the spoon remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一块方糖从边缘缩小，最后只剩勺子。

abstract.en: Picture a knot pulled strand by strand until the rope lies flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被一缕一缕拉开，直到绳子摊平。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd at a station thinning until the platform is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象站台上的人群渐渐变少，最后空无一人。

examples.cn: 药片在半杯水里溶开。

examples.en: The board voted to dissolve the charity and return its funds.
examples.cn: 董事会投票决定解散该慈善机构并退还资金。

examples.en: The crowd dissolved once the music stopped.
examples.cn: 音乐一停，人群就散了。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one loosening: a solid melts into a liquid, a cook makes it happen, a firm is untied, a contract released, a fog fades, composure collapses, suspicion clears, a film image fades into the next, and water takes stone apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一种松开：固体进入液体、厨师促成此事、公司被解开、契约被解除、雾散去、镇定崩掉、疑虑消除、影像淡入下一格、水把石头拆走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar cube losing its edges in warm water until no outline is left at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：方糖在温水里失去边缘，杯底再找不到轮廓。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL CORE: bonds between particles loosen, with or without a named doer.
branches.cn: 物质核心：粒子间的联结松开，不论有没有点明作用者。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PICTURE: an organisation or a binding agreement is untied and formally ended.
branches.cn: 法律图景：组织或有约束力的协议被解开并正式终止。

branches.en: THE LOST OUTLINE: fog thins, and one film image loses its edges as another gains them.
branches.cn: 失去轮廓：雾变薄，一个电影画面失去边缘时另一个取得边缘。

branches.en: THE HELD COMPOSURE: composure is a shape too, and it can melt into laughter or tears.
branches.cn: 维持的镇定：镇定也是一种形状，也会融化进笑声或眼泪。

branches.en: THE SLOW WORK: suspicion clears like a solid, and groundwater takes limestone apart over ages.
branches.cn: 缓慢的作用：怀疑像固体一样消失，地下水在漫长岁月里把石灰岩拆走。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere gives solve, resolve, absolve and dissolution, while dis- also appears in divide, disperse and dissent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere 衍生 solve、resolve、absolve 与 dissolution，而 dis- 也出现在 divide、disperse 与 dissent 中。
